decisions.decision: SM-2 must be implemented as a pure, dependency-free module with an injected Calendar/clock, and its exact formula (ease update, 1.3 floor, Hard's effect, lapse reset behavior) must be written as a spec with worked numeric examples before any code is written.
decisions.rationale: "SM-2" is not a single unambiguous spec across implementations (Anki vs. SuperMemo vs. others differ on lapse and ease handling); without a pre-committed spec, tests would just describe whatever got coded, defeating 'provably right, not plausibly right.'
rejected_alternatives: Implement first and write tests against the implementation
Follow Anki's specific SM-2 variant without documenting the choice
constraints: No `Date()`/`Calendar.current` calls inside the SM-2 module
Spec with worked examples must exist before scheduler code is written

decisions.decision: Due-date arithmetic is evaluated as calendar-day math against the current device calendar at query time, not as a frozen instant comparison, and tests must cover a simulated DST transition and a simulated mid-interval timezone change.
decisions.rationale: Comparing raw instants breaks silently across DST and timezone changes even though 'a day' is defined as a calendar day; only query-time calendar math plus deterministic clock injection makes this provable rather than assumed.
rejected_alternatives: Store and compare absolute due Date instants only
Treat timezone-change handling as out of scope
constraints: Day-boundary tests must simulate device timezone change and DST, not just midnight rollover

decisions.decision: Each card's grade is persisted immediately per-card during a review session, and the session summary screen is only shown for a session that actually completed — never fabricated for an interrupted one.
decisions.rationale: The prompt's 'quitting mid-session loses nothing' is a strong claim that only holds if persistence is per-card and immediate; showing a summary for an incomplete session would violate the no-false-success rule.
rejected_alternatives: Batch-persist grades at session end
Reconstruct a fake summary on relaunch after a crash
constraints: Verification method: force-quit simulator mid-session, confirm graded cards updated and ungraded cards still due on relaunch

decisions.decision: CSV import must enumerate and surface a visible per-row error for every malformed-row case (empty front/back, wrong column count, embedded commas/quotes, bad encoding/BOM, CRLF vs LF, duplicates), and export→import must round-trip losslessly.
decisions.rationale: The prompt's 'never silently drop a row' is only checkable if every failure mode is explicitly enumerated and tested rather than left to implicit parser behavior.
rejected_alternatives: Best-effort parsing that coerces or skips ambiguous rows
Only handle the happy path and treat edge cases as out of scope
constraints: Every listed malformed-row case must produce a distinct, visible per-row error in the preview step

decisions.decision: The daily reminder's due-count is recomputed at natural refresh points (foreground, background, post-session, day rollover) rather than fixed at scheduling time, and no notification fires on a 0-due day.
decisions.rationale: A scheduled local notification's body text is fixed at schedule time on iOS, so a static 'N cards due' would go stale; firing a '0 cards due' notification also contradicts the prompt's explicit priority on honest empty states.
rejected_alternatives: Schedule the notification body once with the count at schedule time
Always fire the notification regardless of due count
constraints: No notification is scheduled/fired when computed due count is 0

decisions.decision: No UI affordance of any kind (including disabled/greyed-out controls) may exist for out-of-scope infrastructure-dependent features; each is instead documented as an explicit gap with an effort note in a discoverable location (docs and/or in-app About/Settings).
decisions.rationale: A disabled 'Sync' toggle is itself a misleading claim about what the app does, violating the hard rule against faking or stubbing infrastructure-dependent features.
rejected_alternatives: Greyed-out or 'coming soon' controls for cloud/sync/marketplace features
Gaps documented only in code comments
constraints: Gap register must be in a reviewer-visible location, not buried in source comments

decisions.decision: Conflict tiebreaker order for all later phases is fixed: SM-2 correctness above all, then review-flow speed, then honest empty states.
decisions.rationale: This is the explicit priority order given in the original prompt; later phases need a non-negotiable tiebreaker rather than defaulting to aesthetics or majority vote under time pressure.
rejected_alternatives: Resolve tradeoffs case-by-case without a fixed order
Let UI polish take precedence when schedules are tight
constraints: Any resource-crunch tradeoff must cite this order explicitly

decisions.decision: Non-goals are locked: no cloud sync/iCloud, no accounts, no push, no community/shared decks, no marketplace, no media/markdown/image/audio cards, no sub-deck nesting, no ML-based scheduling beyond SM-2.
decisions.rationale: These all require infrastructure or scope explicitly excluded by the prompt's hard offline-only, native-only constraints.
rejected_alternatives: Allow partial/local-only stand-ins for these features (e.g., local-only 'sharing' via file export mislabeled as sharing)
constraints: Any of these appearing in later designs must be rejected and redirected to the gap register

decisions.decision: Design tokens (type, spacing, color) live in a single Theme.swift referenced everywhere, with full dark-mode support via semantic color roles, and every reachable screen implements empty/loading/success/error states as applicable.
decisions.rationale: Matches the global app-build rules on centralized theming and mandatory UI states; prevents scattered literals and inconsistent or missing state handling across screens.
rejected_alternatives: Per-screen ad hoc styling
Deferring dark mode or empty-state design to a later polish pass
constraints: No font/size/color literals outside Theme.swift
Dark mode verified in both appearances before completion

decisions.decision: Whether demo-seeded decks count toward the user's real stats/streaks, or must be visibly separated from them, is left as an explicit open question for the design phase to resolve unambiguously — not decided in this phase.
decisions.rationale: All three participants touched on demo-data behavior but none proposed a specific resolution; forcing a guess here risks silently deciding something the user didn't specify.
rejected_alternatives: Assume demo decks always count toward real stats
Assume demo decks are always excluded from real stats
constraints: Design phase must state this explicitly and make the boundary visible in-app, whichever way it's resolved

decisions.decision: Target audience is self-directed offline-first learners (language, exam/certification, professional drilling) who likely already tried Anki/Quizlet and specifically want zero-setup, zero-account, guaranteed-offline operation — a narrow niche, not a mass-market product.
decisions.rationale: All three independent passes converged on this same profile from the prompt's offline-only, no-account, no-social constraints; this audience will judge the app against their existing SRS literacy, raising the bar on perceived scheduling correctness.
rejected_alternatives: Positioning as a broad mass-market study app competing on content breadth or social features
constraints: Design and later phases should not spend effort on virality/social/gamification features even if easy to add — audience does not value them and non-goals already exclude them

decisions.decision: Comparable apps are Anki, Quizlet, and secondarily Memrise/Brainscape/RemNote, all cited as ASSUMPTION (no external research fetched); Recall's differentiation is being a deterministic, provably-correct, zero-infrastructure 'reliable review engine' rather than competing on content discovery, social features, or configuration depth.
decisions.rationale: Consistent competitor read across all three contributors gives a concrete, defensible positioning wedge without requiring unsourced factual claims to be presented as fact.
rejected_alternatives: Presenting competitor claims as researched fact instead of labeled assumptions
constraints: Any competitor claim used in later phases must retain its ASSUMPTION label unless real research is performed

decisions.decision: The SM-2 worked-examples spec (already required by the prior phase) must additionally cross-check its output against a widely-trusted external reference case (e.g., Anki's known interval progression for repeated Good grades from a 2.5 starting ease), not merely be internally self-consistent.
decisions.rationale: This audience has used Anki/SuperMemo-derived tools before and will notice if scheduling 'feels wrong' even when the app is internally consistent with its own spec; internal consistency alone is a weaker claim than 'provably right.'
rejected_alternatives: Accepting internal self-consistency of the spec as sufficient proof of correctness
constraints: Design phase's SM-2 spec must include at least one worked example cross-checked against a known external SRS reference case

decisions.decision: The Deck/Card/ReviewLog SwiftData schema should be treated as a design decision to get right early and change rarely, not iterated on casually after the demo-data toggle or review history exists.
decisions.rationale: SwiftData migration handling is a known rough edge; a mishandled migration could silently corrupt or drop review history, which this correctness-sensitive audience would notice immediately.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the schema as freely iterable throughout the build and handling migration issues if/when they arise
constraints: Design phase must finalize the core schema shape before dependent features (review session, stats, CSV) are built against it

decisions.decision: Notification due-count staleness between app refresh points is accepted as a documented platform limitation rather than something the build attempts to fix via background refresh tasks.
decisions.rationale: BGAppRefreshTask execution is not guaranteed by iOS without push infrastructure, which this project explicitly excludes; attempting to over-promise reliable background freshness would violate the same honesty principle driving the gap register.
rejected_alternatives: Attempting to use BGAppRefreshTask or similar background execution to keep the notification count fresh without user interaction
constraints: Gap/limitations documentation must explicitly state that due-counts may go stale if the app isn't opened between scheduled refresh points

decisions.decision: CSV import test fixtures must include at least one real-world exported CSV (e.g., from Excel, Numbers, or an Anki export) in addition to hand-crafted edge-case fixtures.
decisions.rationale: Hand-crafted edge cases tend to cluster around what the author already anticipated; real-world exports surface quoting/encoding quirks that a spec written in the abstract is likely to miss.
rejected_alternatives: Relying solely on hand-crafted fixtures designed to hit the enumerated malformed-row cases
constraints: Build/test phase must source or construct at least one realistic, non-synthetic CSV fixture for import testing

decisions.decision: First-build sequencing is: SM-2 module + full test suite (standalone, demoable before any UI) → frozen SwiftData models → interruption-safe review session → stats → CSV export/import → local reminders last; if time is constrained, CSV import is trimmed first (export retained).
decisions.rationale: This ordering matches risk, not breadth — it proves the highest-risk, highest-trust component first and defers the most cuttable, most tolerant-of-being-smaller feature (notifications) to last, consistent with 'smaller finished app over larger half-built.'
rejected_alternatives: Building screens/UI in parallel with the SM-2 module
Treating all six core features as equally sequenced/parallel work
constraints: Design phase must produce the SM-2 spec and its tests before any dependent SwiftUI screen is designed in detail

decisions.decision: Recall is built as a single iOS app (slug: recall-ios); no portfolio split, no sibling child projects, no portfolio-json manifest is produced.
decisions.rationale: The prompt specifies one named app with one integrated feature set (decks/cards, SM-2, review session, stats, CSV, reminders) that all depend on a single local SwiftData store and one due-card query; there is no request for multiple apps, categories, or options, and prior phases already locked a single sequenced build order (SM-2 first, frozen schema, review session, stats, CSV, reminders last) that only coheres as one app.
rejected_alternatives: Splitting into feature-aligned sibling apps (e.g., separate CSV utility app, stats companion app)
Portfolio variants implying backend/infra (Recall Core, Recall Companion, Recall Web API)
Multiple product variants exploring social/sharing/marketplace angles
constraints: No portfolio-json manifest is required or produced for this phase
Any later phase proposing to spin off a feature (e.g., CSV import, stats) into a separate app must be rejected as violating this decision
Single-app status does not reduce scope or rigor — SM-2-first sequencing and frozen-schema discipline from prior phases still apply in full

decisions.decision: Product promise is locked as: Recall is an offline iOS flashcard app that shows you exactly which cards are due today and never lies to you about your progress.
decisions.rationale: All three independent passes converged on this same one-sentence framing (correctness + honesty over feature breadth), matching the SM-2-first, honest-empty-states priorities already fixed in prior phases.
rejected_alternatives: Framing the promise around feature breadth or polish rather than correctness/honesty
constraints: Any proposed feature in later phases must be justifiable as serving this promise or it is out of scope

decisions.decision: Primary user is a self-directed offline-first learner (language/exam/certification/professional drilling), likely ex-Anki/Quizlet, and the defining scenario is a mid-review interruption (call, force-quit, OS kill) that must resolve with zero data loss on reopen.
decisions.rationale: Consistent across all three contributions and directly operationalizes DEC-prompt_contract-003's per-card persistence requirement into a concrete test scenario.
rejected_alternatives: Treating interruption-safety as a nice-to-have rather than the defining design scenario
constraints: Design and build phases must treat the interrupted-session scenario as the primary UX correctness bar for the review screen

decisions.decision: Core loop is locked as: deck list (with due counts) -> pick deck or Study All -> review (reveal, grade, immediate per-card persistence) -> session summary -> back to deck list; stats, CSV, and reminders are satellite features reachable around this loop, not embedded in it.
decisions.rationale: All three contributions independently described the same sequence; keeping stats/CSV/reminders as satellites ensures a user who never opens them still gets full core value, consistent with 'smaller finished app over larger half-built.'
rejected_alternatives: Embedding stats or CSV steps into the review loop itself
constraints: A user must be able to complete the full core loop without ever visiting Stats, CSV, or Settings

decisions.decision: Hard scope boundaries are reaffirmed and extended: in addition to the prior-phase non-goals (no cloud/accounts/push/community decks/marketplace/media cards/sub-decks/ML scheduling), no cross-deck merge or dedup logic and no auto-tagging or 'smart' difficulty inference beyond what SM-2 itself produces.
decisions.rationale: The Design Lead flagged that 'polish' temptations could introduce a whole new correctness surface (smart suggestions, auto-tagging) unrelated to the SM-2 core; no participant objected, and it's consistent with the narrow, correctness-first scope already locked.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing local-only 'smart' convenience features on the grounds that they don't require infrastructure
constraints: Any later phase proposing auto-tagging, smart recommendations, or cross-deck logic must be rejected as scope creep

decisions.decision: Demo-seeded decks are visibly tagged everywhere they appear (deck list, review header, stats breakdowns), excluded by default from overall/aggregate stats and any streak calculation, viewable individually if the user drills into that specific demo deck, and fully removable via one Settings action with no residue left in real stats.
decisions.rationale: Resolves the open question deferred by DEC-prompt_contract-010: blending demo reviews into real retention/streak numbers would make it impossible to show a real user's honest first-time empty state, contradicting the project's explicit priority on honest empty states.
rejected_alternatives: Demo decks always counting toward real stats
Demo decks always fully excluded even from their own per-deck view
constraints: Demo-data visual tagging must appear on every screen where demo decks/cards/stats could appear
Turning off demo data must leave zero trace in real stats or streaks

decisions.decision: Measurable success criteria for this build are the seven items listed in the Final Output (SM-2 correctness + external cross-check, force-quit data-loss test, six screens with real empty states, real-fixture CSV round-trip with per-row errors, zero-due-day notification suppression, demo-data isolation, full airplane-mode run with no crashes).
decisions.rationale: Synthesizes the measurable criteria independently proposed by all three participants into one concrete, testable checklist so 'done' has an objective bar rather than being declared on a partial UI pass.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving success criteria as qualitative statements without concrete pass/fail tests
constraints: The app must not be declared done until each of the seven criteria is demonstrated, per the global rule against declaring done before build verification agrees

decisions.decision: Target user is a serious daily offline studier with 300-3,000 atomic facts (language/exam/cert/professional), likely ex-Anki/Quizlet, who will notice immediately if scheduling or stats are dishonest.
decisions.rationale: All three contributions converged on this same profile, sharpening the audience already locked in earlier phases with a concrete scale (card-count range) that grounds the free-tier caps decided in this phase.
rejected_alternatives: Casual/occasional flashcard user as primary persona
constraints: Free-tier caps and premium value must be sized against this daily, at-scale user, not a casual one

decisions.decision: Recall Free includes the complete, fully correct core loop (SM-2, review sessions, CSV import/export, stats) forever, capped only at 3 decks / 300 real (non-demo) cards and 30 days of stats history plus the 30-day forecast; Recall Plus is a subscription that removes those caps and adds per-deck local reminder-time customization.
decisions.rationale: Gives 'subscription value is functional, not cosmetic' a concrete, buildable answer while keeping every locked core-loop requirement (SM-2 correctness, review speed, CSV import) fully free, since gating those would violate the fixed SM-2>speed>honesty priority order and the CSV import contract.
rejected_alternatives: Gating review-flow speed or keyboard-friendly card editing behind a paywall (Codex's authoring-suite proposal)
Cosmetic-only premium unlocks (icon packs, themes)
Fully uncapped free tier with no monetization hook
Unlimited demo decks as a paid feature (Gemini fallback) — demo data is a single reversible seed toggle, not a scalable resource
constraints: No core correctness, scheduling accuracy, or review-flow speed feature may be paywalled
CSV import/export functionality itself stays fully free regardless of plan

decisions.decision: A lapsed Recall Plus subscription never deletes or hides any deck, card, or review history already created; it only blocks creating new decks/cards beyond the free caps until the user resubscribes or trims back under the cap.
decisions.rationale: The app's core promise is never lying to the user about their progress; making a user's own study history vanish or go read-only on lapse would be a worse trust violation than anything the original gap-honesty rule addresses.
rejected_alternatives: Hiding over-cap decks/cards until resubscription
Read-only lockout of over-cap content on lapse
constraints: Design and build phases must ensure no data-hiding or read-only lockout logic is ever attached to subscription state

decisions.decision: The App Store purchase transaction is documented as the one explicit, narrow exception to the offline-forever guarantee (an OS-level StoreKit service, not app-initiated networking); all entitlement checks, feature gating, and restore-purchases read from the on-device transaction cache and work fully offline afterward.
decisions.rationale: StoreKit purchases require momentary connectivity like any paid app; pretending otherwise would be dishonest, while treating it as a bug would waste a QA cycle chasing something that isn't one.
rejected_alternatives: Omitting this exception from the gap/limitations doc and letting it be discovered as a 'bug' later
Blocking all monetization to preserve a literal zero-network claim
constraints: Gap/limitations documentation must state this exception explicitly
Verification: airplane-mode test confirms the full app including an already-purchased Plus entitlement works; only the purchase sheet requires network and must fail gracefully with a clear message

decisions.decision: CSV import preview must surface plan-cap-blocked rows as their own distinct, visible reason (e.g., 'not imported: plan limit reached'), separate from malformed-row error categories and never silently truncated, whenever an import would exceed the Free deck/card caps.
decisions.rationale: Extends the already-locked never-silently-drop-a-row discipline (DEC-prompt_contract-004) to the one new failure mode that monetization introduces; without this explicit carry-forward, CSV import would likely be built against the cap as an afterthought.
rejected_alternatives: Silently truncating imports at the cap
Folding cap-blocked rows into the existing malformed-row error categories
constraints: Design phase must specify a distinct visible UI treatment for cap-blocked rows in the CSV import preview

decisions.decision: Competitive wedge is reaffirmed as deterministic, provably-correct, zero-infrastructure reliability, extended explicitly to monetization: no ads, no dark patterns, and no paywalling of correctness or speed.
decisions.rationale: This audience actively distrusts apps that gate correctness behind a paywall; making this an explicit brand commitment protects the trust-first positioning already established.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing limited ads or engagement-driven upsell prompts to subsidize the free tier
constraints: No later phase may introduce ads or manipulative upgrade prompts

decisions.decision: Growth mechanism is CSV file portability (export/AirDrop/Files, cold-import by another user) plus presence in niche learner communities (exam-prep/language subreddits, Discords) and offline-focused App Store search terms; no referral codes, share sheets, or social mechanics are introduced.
decisions.rationale: The app has no accounts, so account-based virality mechanisms don't fit; CSV interoperability is an honest, already-built feature that naturally produces word-of-mouth without inventing a fake social loop.
rejected_alternatives: Referral codes or in-app share sheets
Social media campaign as the primary growth lever (Gemini fallback's vaguer proposal)
constraints: No later phase may add account-based or social sharing mechanics to manufacture virality

decisions.decision: Local-first behavior is confirmed as the v1 architecture with no network dependency beyond the StoreKit purchase exception; any future cloud extension must be strictly additive (optional encrypted remote mirror, immutable card-history events, deterministic conflict policy) and never a v1 requirement.
decisions.rationale: Matches the locked no-backend, offline-forever contract while leaving a concrete, non-hand-wavy path for a future version without requiring any rewrite of the local source-of-truth model.
rejected_alternatives: Designing v1 around an eventual sync layer
Leaving the cloud-ready path unspecified
constraints: Any future sync design must preserve local records as source of truth and use last-write-wins-with-user-resolution or an equivalent deterministic policy, not silent overwrite

decisions.decision: The MVP validation slice is a single deck with fast keyboard-driven card entry, a complete review session (reveal, grade, immediate real SwiftData persistence per card), and a truthful session summary shown only for genuinely completed sessions — built on top of a fully correct, fully tested SM-2 module.
decisions.rationale: All three participants converged on proving the one claim the whole project rests on (trustworthy scheduling and persistence under interruption) rather than building partial breadth across many features; a wrong interval or lossy persistence at this stage would invalidate the entire premise regardless of what else gets built.
rejected_alternatives: Building a thinner review loop with a stubbed or partially-correct SM-2 implementation
Simulating persistence in-memory to move faster on the UI
constraints: Real SwiftData persistence is required even at this minimal scope — no in-memory simulation
SM-2 unit tests must pass before any review screen code ships

decisions.decision: The force-quit-mid-session interruption test (graded cards persisted and off the due stack, ungraded cards still due, no fabricated summary) is the single defining validation interaction for this phase.
decisions.rationale: This is the concrete scenario ex-Anki/Quizlet users have been burned by before and the moment that proves 'never lies to you about your progress' rather than merely asserting it.
rejected_alternatives: Treating interruption-safety as a nice-to-have validated later alongside stats/CSV work
constraints: This test must be demonstrated (scripted or manual) before the slice is considered validated

decisions.decision: The demo-data toggle is NOT built in this slice as a real Settings feature; only a throwaway internal seed path may be used if needed to avoid demoing against an empty deck.
decisions.rationale: Two of three participants (Codex, Claude) independently excluded it, and the reasoning holds: real demo-data isolation depends on aggregate stats existing to be excluded from, and stats are explicitly cut from this slice — building the toggle now would mean building it against features that don't exist yet.
rejected_alternatives: Building the full demo-data toggle with visual tagging now, as proposed by Gemini's fallback pass
constraints: Any seed/demo path used in this slice is internal/throwaway only, not the user-facing Settings toggle described in the original prompt

decisions.decision: Dark mode via semantic Theme.swift color roles is NOT cut for this slice and must be verified in both appearances even at minimal scope.
decisions.rationale: Full dark-mode support is a global, non-negotiable app-build rule, not a feature-breadth item that scales with slice size; correcting Gemini's fallback proposal to cut it.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring dark mode support until later polish, as proposed by Gemini's fallback pass
constraints: Later build phases inherit this: dark mode is never on a cut list regardless of scope size

decisions.decision: Full DST/timezone-change SM-2 test breadth is deferred to the dedicated SM-2 build phase; this slice only requires proving the day-boundary mechanism itself via the injected clock with at least one concrete case.
decisions.rationale: Claude's nuance, unopposed: the mechanism must be demonstrably correct now, but exhaustive DST/timezone-change coverage is appropriately sequenced into the phase that builds the SM-2 module in full per DEC-prompt_contract-002.
rejected_alternatives: Requiring full DST/timezone-change test coverage before this validation slice can be considered complete
constraints: The full test matrix locked in DEC-prompt_contract-002 still must land before the SM-2 module is considered done overall — this only sequences when within the roadmap

decisions.decision: This phase's output is explicitly a validation slice feeding the already-locked full build sequence (SM-2 -> frozen schema -> review session -> stats -> CSV -> reminders), not a renegotiation of the final app's scope.
decisions.rationale: All three participants flagged the risk that a deliberately narrow slice could be misread as shrinking the eventual app; stating this explicitly prevents that misinterpretation from propagating into later phases.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the slice/roadmap relationship implicit
constraints: Later phases must treat every item on this phase's cut list as deferred, not removed, per the roadmap already locked in product_research

decisions.decision: SM-2 is locked to literal SuperMemo-2 arithmetic (EF' = EF + (0.1 − (5−q)×(0.08+(5−q)×0.02)), EF floored at 1.3; I(1)=1 day, I(2)=6 days, I(n)=round(I(n-1)×EF) for n>2) with an explicit UI grade mapping (Again=q2, Hard=q3, Good=q4, Easy=q5); a lapse is defined as quality<3 (Again only), resetting repetition count to 0 and interval to 1 day while still applying the EF decrease; Hard is a passing grade that advances repetition/interval/EF normally, not a lapse.
decisions.rationale: "SM-2" is not a single unambiguous formula across implementations (Anki diverges from literal SuperMemo-2 on lapse handling and Hard's effect); without pinning one exact variant with a documented grade mapping, two engineers would defensibly build different schedules, defeating 'provably right, not plausibly right.'
rejected_alternatives: Implementing Anki's relearning-steps/configurable lapse-interval-% variant without documenting the choice
Leaving the quality-score mapping for Again/Hard/Good/Easy as an implementation detail decided ad hoc during coding
constraints: The SM-2 spec-with-worked-examples phase must use this exact formula and grade mapping

The external cross-check against Anki's known interval progression (DEC-product_research-003) must explain any visible divergence from Anki's numbers rather than treat it as a bug, since Anki is not literal SM-2

decisions.decision: CSV format is defined as front, back, and an optional third note column (not strictly two-column-only) so that export-then-import is genuinely lossless, including notes.
decisions.rationale: DEC-prompt_contract-004 requires lossless round-trip, but a strictly two-column importer would silently drop a card's note on re-import since notes are part of the card model and appear in export — that is exactly the 'never silently drop data' failure this feature exists to prevent.
rejected_alternatives: Redefining 'lossless round-trip' to mean only front/back and documenting note loss as an accepted limitation
Keeping import strictly two-column as literally worded in the original prompt
constraints: CSV import must validate front/back as required per existing malformed-row rules while treating the note column as optional per-row (absent note is not an error)

decisions.decision: Due-status/day-boundary evaluation is an explicit function of (instant, device's current timezone at query time) — including the case where a device timezone change alone flips a card's due status with no review taken — and this is named as an accepted, documented limitation alongside notification staleness.
decisions.rationale: This is the necessary corollary of the already-locked calendar-day-at-query-time rule (DEC-prompt_contract-002), but it is a non-obvious behavior for a 'reliable review engine' claim and needs to be tested and disclosed rather than discovered as a surprise.
rejected_alternatives: Treating timezone-crossing as identical to and covered by the existing DST test case
Leaving timezone-crossing due-status behavior implicit and undocumented
constraints: SM-2/day-boundary test suite must include a dedicated timezone-crossing case distinct from the DST case
Gap/limitations documentation must state that due status and reminder counts can be affected by device timezone changes

decisions.decision: Per-card grade persistence must use an explicit, synchronous context.save() call at grade time, never relying on ModelContext.autosaveEnabled.
decisions.rationale: Autosave batches on a timer/scene-phase basis and would reopen the exact data-loss window the interruption-safety guarantee (DEC-prompt_contract-003) exists to close; SQLite's atomic commit protects the database's integrity but not an in-memory grade that autosave hasn't flushed yet.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on SwiftData's default autosave behavior for per-grade persistence
constraints: Review session architecture must call an explicit save after each grade before advancing to the next card
The force-quit interruption test must include a kill timed at/immediately after the save call, not only between UI taps

decisions.decision: Information architecture is locked as a 3-tab shell: Study (deck list, due counts, review entry), Stats, and Settings & Tools (CSV import/export, reminders, demo-data toggle, subscription/plan status, gap/limitations register).
decisions.rationale: Keeps the core loop one tap away while making satellite features discoverable without cluttering the primary flow, consistent with DEC-initial_discussion-003's satellite-feature framing.
rejected_alternatives: A deeper or more fragmented navigation with separate top-level destinations for CSV, reminders, and subscription
constraints: Design phase must produce screen designs against this 3-tab structure

decisions.decision: CSV duplicate detection is defined as a case-sensitive exact front+back match, checked both within the imported file and against existing non-archived cards in the target deck, surfaced as its own distinct per-row reason separate from malformed-row and plan-cap-blocked categories.
decisions.rationale: 'Duplicate' was named as a failure mode in DEC-prompt_contract-004 but never defined precisely enough to implement or test consistently.
rejected_alternatives: Fuzzy or case-insensitive duplicate matching
Silently merging or silently skipping duplicate rows
constraints: Import preview UI must show a distinct reason string for duplicate rows, never folded into malformed-row or cap-blocked categories

decisions.decision: Archived decks and their cards continue to count against Free-tier caps (3 decks/300 cards); card deletion is in scope as part of card editing, and deleting a card cascades to delete its ReviewLog history, which can retroactively change retention-rate stats as expected, honest behavior.
decisions.rationale: Archiving is not deletion, so excluding archived content from the cap would let users trivially evade it, undermining DEC-per_app_product_brief-002; 'edit cards' implicitly requires delete to be usable, and cascading the ReviewLog is the only interpretation consistent with never retaining or fabricating orphaned data.
rejected_alternatives: Excluding archived decks/cards from cap counting
Treating card deletion as out of scope for this app
Preserving orphaned ReviewLog rows after a card is deleted
constraints: Build phase must implement cap counting inclusive of archived content
Card deletion must cascade-delete its ReviewLog; retroactive stat changes after deletion are expected behavior, not a defect to fix

decisions.decision: Grading controls (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) must be distinguishable without relying on color alone, and the daily local reminder's notification body must contain only a numeric due-card count — never card content, deck names, or subject matter.
decisions.rationale: Color-only grading buttons fail color-blind and VoiceOver users, and accessibility is already a stated product requirement, not polish; lock-screen notification previews are visible to anyone glancing at a shared device, so leaking study content would be a real privacy regression.
rejected_alternatives: Color-coded-only grading buttons (red/orange/green/blue) with no additional distinguishing label
Richer notification text naming specific decks or subjects
constraints: Grading UI must include distinct text labels and/or accessible VoiceOver labels per grade, not glyph/color alone
Notification body text generation must never interpolate card or deck content, only the numeric due count

decisions.decision: The SwiftData store's participation in normal OS-level iCloud device backup is acknowledged as consistent with the offline-forever contract (it is OS-initiated, not app-initiated sync); no cross-device merge logic exists if a user restores diverging backups onto two devices, and this must be documented explicitly in the gap/limitations register.
decisions.rationale: This is a predictable support question for a daily, at-scale, possibly multi-device user, and it is consistent with the already-locked no-cross-deck-merge/no-v1-sync non-goals, but needs to be named rather than silently left undiscovered.
rejected_alternatives: Pretending no backup/restore divergence scenario exists
Building ad hoc merge/conflict resolution for this scenario in v1, which would contradict DEC-per_app_product_brief-008's no-v1-sync rule
constraints: Gap/limitations documentation must state that OS-level device backup/restore across two devices can produce diverging, unmerged local stores

decisions.decision: Feature prioritization is locked to MoSCoW with eleven must-have feature groups (SM-2 engine, deck/card CRUD, interruption-safe review session, stats, CSV import/export, local reminders, demo-data toggle, Theme/dark-mode, gap register, Free/Plus gating, non-color-dependent grading accessibility), two should-haves (3-tab IA, search/filter), one could-have (advanced chart interactions), and a hard won't-build list (cloud/accounts/marketplace/social/media-cards/sub-decks/ML-scheduling/cross-deck-dedupe/ads).
decisions.rationale: Both substantive contributors (Codex, Claude) independently produced near-identical must/should/could/won't breakdowns compiling every requirement already locked in prior phases into a gradable list; convergence without contradiction on this much surface area is a strong signal the scope line is correct.
rejected_alternatives: Treating any of the eleven must-haves as should-have to reduce build risk
Scoring 3-tab IA and search/filter as must-have rather than should-have
constraints: Every future phase must treat the eleven must-have groups as non-negotiable completion gates
The won't-build list may not gain any UI affordance, including disabled controls, per the already-locked DEC-prompt_contract-006

decisions.decision: Per-deck local reminder-time customization is locked as its own explicit must-have requirement, not left implicit inside general Free/Plus gating.
decisions.rationale: It is the only functional feature Plus adds per DEC-per_app_product_brief-002; if it is allowed to slip to should-have under build pressure, the monetization decision from that phase becomes unbuildable and Plus has zero differentiation.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving per-deck reminder customization as an implicit detail under the general Free/Plus requirement
constraints: Build phase must implement per-deck reminder-time customization as a gating must-have, not a stretch goal

decisions.decision: Every must-have acceptance criterion must be independently executable by a human or script to a pass/fail result — restating the feature description is not an acceptance criterion.
decisions.rationale: Without this discipline, 'acceptance criteria' risk becoming decorative prose that can't actually gate a build-verification pass, undermining the project's 'provably right, not plausibly right' standard.
rejected_alternatives: Accepting qualitative/descriptive acceptance criteria for must-have features
constraints: Requirements-json entries and later build verification must map to concrete, checkable tests or scripted scenarios

decisions.decision: Two new concrete acceptance checks are added to the must-have gate: CSV test fixtures must include at least one real-world exported file (not only hand-crafted edge cases), and hitting a Free-tier cap mid-review-session must not corrupt or block the in-progress session.
decisions.rationale: The first operationalizes DEC-product_research-006 into a testable gate rather than a suggestion; the second closes a previously unstated interaction between monetization caps and the review-flow-speed priority, which the fixed SM-2>speed>honesty tiebreaker (DEC-prompt_contract-007) requires be protected.
rejected_alternatives: Treating real-world CSV fixtures as a nice-to-have rather than a gating test
Leaving cap-during-review behavior unspecified and discovering it as a bug during build
constraints: Build/test phase must source or construct a real-world CSV fixture and include a cap-hit-mid-session test case

decisions.decision: The 3-tab information architecture (already locked structurally in DEC-detailed_discussion-005) is scored as should-have rather than must-have within this phase's MoSCoW prioritization, meaning it does not itself gate 'done' even though it will be built as the locked navigational shell.
decisions.rationale: MoSCoW scoring in this phase measures what gates completion under time pressure, not what is architecturally decided; the IA is already structurally locked and not actually at risk of being cut, so should-have scoring reflects prioritization nuance, not a reopening of the IA decision.
rejected_alternatives: Scoring 3-tab IA as must-have, duplicating the prior lock as a redundant gate
constraints: The 3-tab IA decision itself remains locked per DEC-detailed_discussion-005; should-have scoring here is about build-priority sequencing only, not about whether it gets built

decisions.decision: Design language is named 'The Honest Ledger': a calm, information-dense, non-gamified visual language (tabular numerals for counts, ink/graphite palette with a single reserved amber accent used only for due-today badges and confirmed-save moments).
decisions.rationale: Codex and Claude independently converged on the same underlying philosophy (precision-instrument trust over engagement/gamification); Claude's persona-grounded framing and concrete palette were adopted as the more specific, buildable version of the same direction.
rejected_alternatives: Codex's 'Scheduled Trust Instrument' naming (same philosophy, folded in rather than kept as a separate competing name)
Generic 'clean and modern' non-answer
Gamified/streak-flame/confetti visual register
constraints: Any later phase or build artifact must reference this name and palette rationale, not invent a new unrelated design language

decisions.decision: The default-looking version of this app (plain List rows, stock Form, system blue accent, color-only grade pills, generic unlabeled charts, post-grade 'Saved!' toast) is explicitly rejected with five named concrete replacements: custom due-count deck cards, ascending-staircase shape/position/label-based grading buttons, ink/graphite+amber palette with no system blue, directly-labeled 'today' bar in the forecast chart, and structural (not toast-based) save confirmation.
decisions.rationale: The phase rules require explicit rejection of the default look with named differences, not adjectives; the toast-banner rejection is additionally a correctness requirement, not just aesthetic preference, since a 'Saved' banner mid-session risks implying false session completion.
rejected_alternatives: Default SwiftUI List/Form/TabView chrome
Color-only (red/orange/green/blue) grading buttons with no shape/label distinction
A green 'Saved!' toast/banner shown after each grade
constraints: No screen may ship with default unstyled List/Form chrome where this spec calls for custom rows/cards
No completion-implying confirmation UI (toast, banner, checkmark overlay) may appear after a single grade during an active session

decisions.decision: Signature interaction is the reveal-and-grade motion: a fast (<200ms), no-bounce content settle on tap-to-reveal (explicitly not a 3D card-flip), paired with four grade buttons rising from the bottom edge, each with a distinct haptic weight on an ascending ladder from Again to Easy.
decisions.rationale: Expresses the design language's calm/trust register while protecting review-flow speed (priority #2); a literal card-flip looks nice once but is fatiguing by the fortieth card of a session, and the haptic ladder lets grading work by feel for a user reviewing one-handed on a moving train.
rejected_alternatives: A literal 3D card-flip reveal animation
Uniform/no haptic feedback across all four grade buttons
constraints: Reduced-motion accessibility setting must disable the reveal-settle animation but must not remove the haptic ladder, since haptics are not motion

decisions.decision: Screen inventory is locked across the existing 3-tab shell: Study (Deck List w/ due counts + Study All + empty/all-caught-up states; Deck Detail; Card Editor sheet with keyboard-first flow; Review Session; Session Summary reachable only on full completion), Stats (Overview + per-deck drill-down, each with distinct empty/sparse/success states), Settings & Tools (root list; CSV Export; CSV Import with per-row status preview; Reminders with tri-state permission handling and per-deck Plus override; Demo Data toggle; Plan/Subscription screen; Gap & Limitations register as its own real screen).
decisions.rationale: Both substantive contributors independently produced nearly identical screen inventories mapped onto the already-locked 3-tab IA; Claude's version added concrete detail (Study All entry, cap-hit-mid-session as inline notice not modal, Gap register as a first-class readable screen rather than a buried settings row) that Codex did not contradict.
rejected_alternatives: Burying the Gap & Limitations register inside a generic settings row rather than giving it its own screen
A modal interruption for the cap-hit-mid-session case
constraints: Build phase must implement each listed screen with the state model specified in DEC-design_discussion-005
The Gap & Limitations register must be reachable as its own discoverable screen, not nested prose in an About page

decisions.decision: Per-screen state models are locked, including two new explicit substates beyond prior phases' requirements: Deck List gets a distinct 'all caught up' success substate separate from true empty, and Review Session gets a 'cap hit mid-session' state rendered as a small non-blocking inline notice rather than a modal.
decisions.rationale: A true-empty state ('you have no decks yet') and an 'all caught up' state ('you have decks but nothing is due') communicate very different things and deserve different copy; rendering the cap-hit state as a modal would itself violate the locked requirement that hitting a cap must not corrupt or interrupt an in-progress review session.
rejected_alternatives: Reusing one generic empty-state graphic for both true-empty and all-caught-up cases
A modal/blocking alert for the cap-hit-mid-session case
constraints: Stats screens must never render a chart from fabricated-looking flat placeholder data even in the sparse state

decisions.decision: Accessibility requirements for this phase are locked as: grading buttons satisfy the non-color-dependent requirement specifically via the shape/position/label staircase (not a later-added tooltip); card front/back text scales with Dynamic Type including accessibility sizes via a scrolling card area, with the grade-button area reserved in the bottom safe zone; charts carry Swift Charts accessibility summary labels.
decisions.rationale: Claude flagged that the staircase/haptic-ladder approach is more visually and technically interesting than four equal buttons and risks being treated as stretch polish and cut under build-time pressure, when it is in fact how the already-locked non-color-dependent grading requirement gets satisfied.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the staircase layout as optional visual polish rather than the accessibility requirement's actual implementation
Letting Dynamic Type growth push grade buttons off-screen
constraints: Build phase may not substitute a plain tooltip or color-only fallback for the staircase layout and call the accessibility requirement satisfied

decisions.decision: A single canonical token set (type scale, spacing grid, color palette, corner radii) is locked from Codex's fuller semantic palette (covers surfaceMuted/Elevated, textTertiary, chartGrid, focusOutline — roles Claude's independently-derived palette didn't name), reconciling it with Claude's compatible-but-different hex values.
decisions.rationale: Both contributors produced complete, numerically-specified specs in the same direction (Honest Ledger, ink/graphite/amber) but with different exact hex values since they worked independently; a build needs one canonical file, not two options.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping Claude's palette instead (fewer named semantic roles for required categories like chart grid and focus outline)
Leaving both palettes in the handoff for the builder to choose
constraints: Theme.swift must be built from the values in this phase's Final Output only, with zero invented values
No color/font/spacing literal may appear outside Theme.swift

decisions.decision: Component inventory is merged into one canonical named list, with three components explicitly flagged as their own files that must not be reimplemented ad hoc: GradeStaircase (neutral ink/graphite only, no per-grade color), DemoDataTag (one reusable component used everywhere demo content appears), and InlineCapNotice (persistent, non-blocking, shaped distinctly from anything toast-like).
decisions.rationale: Both contributors independently converged on nearly the same component set; the explicit do-not-regress flag on these three specifically protects already-locked accessibility (DEC-design_discussion-006) and correctness (no false-completion signal) requirements that are easy for a builder to quietly erode under time pressure.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving component boundaries implicit and letting the builder infer which pieces are load-bearing vs. cosmetic
constraints: A future change adding per-grade color tinting or a toast-style save confirmation is a regression against this decision, not a style choice

decisions.decision: Navigation is locked as three independent per-tab NavigationStacks; Review Session pushes onto the Study stack (not a sheet) and hides the tab bar for its duration; Card Editor, CSV Import, and Plan/Subscription present as sheets; Session Summary is a sheet reachable only after true queue completion; the in-session exit control reads 'End session — your progress is saved' rather than a loss-warning dialog.
decisions.rationale: Claude's specific mechanism (push + hidden tab bar to protect focus during the highest-stakes flow) refines Codex's less specific navigation description without contradicting it; the honest exit-copy detail is required because, given the locked interruption-safety architecture, a loss-warning dialog would literally be lying to the user.
rejected_alternatives: Presenting Review Session as a sheet
A confirmation dialog warning the user they might lose progress by leaving early
constraints: Build phase must implement the exit control's copy exactly as specified, since it is a correctness statement, not just UX copy

decisions.decision: Review Session must snapshot an ordered array of due Card IDs once at session start and step through it by index — it must NOT be driven by a live SwiftData @Query.
decisions.rationale: A live query re-triggers on every grade (since grading mutates dueDate), which can reorder or shrink the visible queue mid-session, especially in Study All mode across multiple decks — this would look exactly like a data-loss bug even though the underlying data is safe, and it is the kind of subtle pitfall a builder would introduce by reaching for the 'obviously idiomatic' SwiftUI pattern.
rejected_alternatives: Driving the review queue directly off a live @Query for simplicity
constraints: Build/test phase must include a Study-All multi-deck test that would catch queue reordering if this constraint is violated

decisions.decision: Interruption-safety is implemented as 'recompute the due query fresh from truth on relaunch' rather than an explicit session save/restore mechanism; there is no separate persisted resume-point.
decisions.rationale: Because each grade is already synchronously saved and updates the card's dueDate immediately, a fresh due-query on relaunch automatically excludes graded cards and automatically includes ungraded ones — building a separate resume-state mechanism would add its own bug surface for no benefit and risks a path by which a fabricated summary could appear.
rejected_alternatives: Persisting and restoring an explicit session/resume-point object
constraints: The force-quit test scenario should verify this by killing mid-session and confirming the relaunched due query alone produces the correct graded/ungraded split, not a restored session object

decisions.decision: SwiftData schema is finalized as Deck/Card/ReviewLog with the fields specified; Card.isDemo is a denormalized copy from its parent Deck at creation time (not derived via join), due status is a computed predicate against a freshly-computed 'start of tomorrow' instant (never a stored boolean), and ReviewLog rows are strictly append-only and never mutated in place.
decisions.rationale: This is the concrete implementation of the calendar-day-at-query-time rule (DEC-prompt_contract-002) and the cloud-readiness immutable-event-log intent (DEC-per_app_product_brief-008); denormalizing isDemo avoids an expensive join on every stats aggregation at the 300-3,000 card scale this persona lives at, and append-only ReviewLog prevents a future 'quick bug fix' from silently breaking the immutable-history guarantee.
rejected_alternatives: Deriving isDemo via a join to Deck on every query
Storing due status as a mutable boolean flag
Allowing in-place correction of ReviewLog rows
constraints: Build phase must enforce ReviewLog immutability at the architecture level (e.g., no update path exposed), not just as a convention

decisions.decision: Per-grade save runs synchronously on the main actor against the live ModelContext; this is an accepted, explicitly named performance cost (a possible small stutter on old devices), not something to defer to a background save.
decisions.rationale: This is the mechanism that actually closes the interruption-safety guarantee (DEC-detailed_discussion-004); backgrounding the save for a smoother feel would silently reopen the exact data-loss window the app's entire trust claim depends on closing, and given the SM-2-correctness-then-speed-then-honesty tiebreaker, correctness wins this specific tradeoff.
rejected_alternatives: Moving the per-grade save to a background queue/actor for smoother perceived performance
constraints: Any future performance optimization pass must not move this save off the synchronous main-actor path

decisions.decision: Local reminders use repeats:false, re-scheduled (remove-pending then re-add for 'tomorrow') at each of the four locked refresh points; gap-register copy should describe a skipped day as the notification 'never being created,' not merely 'stale.'
decisions.rationale: A UNCalendarNotificationTrigger's body text is fixed at schedule time, so repeats:true would freeze a due-count forever; this refines the already-locked staleness-acceptance decision (DEC-product_research-005) with the actual technically-accurate framing for the gap register.
rejected_alternatives: Using repeats:true with a fixed body text
Keeping the vaguer 'staleness' framing instead of the more accurate 'never created' framing
constraints: Gap & Limitations screen copy must use the 'never created if app unopened between days' framing

decisions.decision: The four-step haptic ladder is concretely mapped onto iOS's actual 5 discrete UIImpactFeedbackGenerator styles as Again=.light, Hard=.medium, Good=.heavy, Easy=.heavy+a second .light pulse — resolving the fact that iOS's styles (light/medium/heavy/soft/rigid) are not a clean linear intensity scale.
decisions.rationale: Codex's original light/medium/rigid/heavy mapping doesn't reliably read as an ascending ladder since rigid and heavy differ in feel-character more than magnitude; Claude's fix gives Easy a distinctly 'extra' top-of-ladder feel using only real, available iOS haptic primitives.
rejected_alternatives: The original light/medium/rigid/heavy mapping
Inventing a fifth intensity level iOS doesn't provide
constraints: Haptic ladder must be validated on a physical device before considered done — Simulator playback is not representative

decisions.decision: No external Claude Design pass is used by default; the spec's explicit numeric values are sufficient for direct SwiftUI implementation. A ready-to-use Claude Design prompt is preserved for optional use only if the run is configured to pause for external design or a limited palette sanity-check is wanted.
decisions.rationale: Every token has a real number and every component is named/mapped; the actual risk in this app is native SwiftUI fidelity (Dynamic Type, safe areas, VoiceOver, haptic timing), not visual concepting, so an external design round would only add reverse-engineering risk without reducing any real uncertainty.
rejected_alternatives: Always running a full external Claude Design mockup pass across all 13 screens
constraints: If external design is invoked, it is scoped to at most Deck List and Review Session as a sanity-check, not a full handoff replacing this document

decisions.decision: App architecture is three layers: a pure domain package (SM-2 engine + CSV parser, zero SwiftUI/SwiftData imports, no direct Date()/Calendar.current calls) as its own local Swift package target, a thin SwiftData repository layer, and SwiftUI + @Observable presentation view models.
decisions.rationale: Physical package separation (not just file-organization convention) is the only thing that reliably prevents a future 'quick fix' from reaching for Date()/Calendar.current directly and silently invalidating the DST/timezone test matrix; it also keeps SM-2 and CSV logic independently testable and provably pure.
rejected_alternatives: Keeping SM-2/CSV as plain files inside the main app target with a style-guide convention against impure calls
A single monolithic app target with MVVM only, no package boundary
constraints: SM-2 and CSV modules must have zero imports of SwiftUI, SwiftData, or Foundation's Date()/Calendar.current singletons — only injected Clock/Calendar values

decisions.decision: Apple framework set is locked to SwiftUI, SwiftData, Swift Charts, StoreKit 2, UserNotifications, UniformTypeIdentifiers, OSLog, Swift Testing, and XCUITest; no ML/CoreML/ARKit or any other framework is introduced.
decisions.rationale: Every locked feature in this app is served by this exact set; nothing in the requirements justifies machine learning, augmented reality, or any framework outside this list, and stating this plainly now prevents tech_specs from re-litigating it.
rejected_alternatives: ML-based scheduling, OCR/handwriting card creation, or card-similarity features using CoreML
constraints: Any framework outside this list requires explicit justification in tech_specs and must still pass the zero-ML/AR non-goal

decisions.decision: ModelContainer initialization must include real error handling with a user-facing recovery screen (retry or explicit start-fresh option) rather than try!, and VersionedSchema/SchemaMigrationPlan scaffolding is set up from v1 even though there is only one schema version today.
decisions.rationale: A try!-based ModelContainer init crash-loops on a corrupted store or failed lightweight migration, which for an app whose entire promise is 'never lose your progress' would be the single worst possible failure mode; setting up migration scaffolding now costs nothing but is the only thing standing between a future required field addition and silently corrupting existing users' ReviewLog history.
rejected_alternatives: Default try! ModelContainer initialization
Deferring migration-plan scaffolding until a second schema version is actually needed
constraints: Build verification must include a test or manual check that a corrupted/unopenable store produces the recovery screen, not a crash

decisions.decision: Exactly one ModelContainer instance exists for the app's entire lifetime, not one per scene or window.
decisions.rationale: Multiple containers/contexts racing on the same underlying store is a real risk under iPad multitasking or any future multi-window scenario, and is trivially avoided by a single shared instance.
rejected_alternatives: Per-scene ModelContainer instances
constraints: Build phase must wire a single app-level ModelContainer, injected via environment, not recreated per view/scene

decisions.decision: The force-quit mid-session interruption test — the single most important test in the app — must be an automated, CI-runnable XCUITest using app.terminate() (a real SIGKILL) at a timed point around the synchronous save, asserting the exact graded/ungraded split on relaunch.
decisions.rationale: A manual-only 'kill the simulator mid-session' QA step bit-rots and can silently stop being performed; app.terminate() is the actual sanctioned XCUITest mechanism for this and must be scripted so 'provably right' doesn't quietly become 'we tried it once.'
rejected_alternatives: Treating the force-quit test as a manual QA checklist item performed once before ship
constraints: This test must exist as a checked-in, CI-runnable XCUITest, not documentation of a manual procedure

decisions.decision: A Privacy Manifest (PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) is a required build-verification checklist item despite the app having zero network calls.
decisions.rationale: Apple's privacy manifest requirement is keyed on API usage categories (e.g. UserDefaults, file timestamps), not network usage, so a zero-network app can still trip App Store review without one; naming this now avoids a late-stage rejection surprise.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming a zero-network app doesn't need a privacy manifest
constraints: Build verification checklist must include confirming PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is present and accurate before submission

decisions.decision: The notification permission prompt fires only when the user actively enables Reminders in Settings, never at cold launch.
decisions.rationale: A denied first-ask at cold launch is much harder to recover from than a contextual ask tied to the user's own action, and this is also better UX consistent with the app's non-nagging tone.
rejected_alternatives: Requesting notification permission at first app launch
constraints: Build phase must gate the UNUserNotificationCenter authorization request behind the user toggling Reminders on, not app launch

decisions.decision: StoreKit implementation requires a checked-in .storekit configuration file with scripted expire/refund/renewal tests, a paywall carrying privacy-policy and terms-of-use links (App Review 3.1.2 requirement for auto-renewing subscriptions), and an explicit bounded error state (not a hang) when a purchase is attempted while offline.
decisions.rationale: These are concrete, easily-missed requirements: the .storekit file makes subscription states testable in Simulator without a sandbox account; the policy/terms links are an actual Apple review requirement, not a nicety; and the offline-purchase case is the one real network touch in an otherwise offline app, so leaving it as a silent spinner would violate the app's own honesty principle.
rejected_alternatives: Testing StoreKit only against a live sandbox account
Leaving the offline-purchase-tap case as an indefinite loading spinner
constraints: Build phase must include a checked-in .storekit config and scripted Xcode StoreKit testing scenarios for expire/refund/renew
Paywall screen must link to privacy policy and terms of use
Purchase flow must show a clear, bounded error message when attempted with no connectivity

decisions.decision: CSV import must wrap file reads from the document picker in startAccessingSecurityScopedResource()/stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource().
decisions.rationale: Document-picker URLs are security-scoped; omitting this pattern works fine in development (same process/session) and then intermittently fails for real users pulling files from iCloud Drive or other Files providers — a classic bug that's easy to miss until it ships.
rejected_alternatives: Reading the picked file URL directly without security-scoped access calls
constraints: CSV import implementation must call start/stopAccessingSecurityScopedResource around every file read from the document picker

decisions.decision: Zero third-party dependencies is reaffirmed as a hard rule; the CSV parser is hand-rolled rather than sourced from any SPM package.
decisions.rationale: The app already has a locked, exhaustive per-row CSV error taxonomy that a generic library wasn't designed around, so hand-rolling is actually less work than fighting someone else's abstraction, while keeping supply-chain surface at zero.
rejected_alternatives: Adopting a third-party CSV parsing library, even a permissively-licensed one
constraints: No new SPM dependency may be added without explicit one-line justification per the approved tech stack policy, and CSV parsing specifically stays hand-rolled

decisions.decision: The Gap & Limitations screen requires its own automated test asserting the screen renders and contains the required disclosure strings (StoreKit exception, notification staleness/never-created framing, timezone-crossing due flips, iCloud backup divergence, full non-goals list).
decisions.rationale: Without an automated check, 'must be documented' is exactly the kind of soft requirement that quietly disappears under time pressure with nobody able to prove it was actually shipped.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on manual review to confirm the Gap & Limitations content is present
constraints: Test suite must include an assertion that the Gap & Limitations screen contains each required disclosure string

decisions.decision: Testing strategy is layered: Swift Testing unit tests for pure domain logic (SM-2, day-boundary/timezone predicates, CSV row classification, cap-hit logic), persistence tests against an in-memory SwiftData container for CRUD/cascade-delete/append-only ReviewLog behavior, integration tests for interruption/reminders/CSV flows, and UI tests paired with deterministic non-UI tests so correctness never depends on animation timing.
decisions.rationale: This maps every locked correctness guarantee (SM-2 purity, interruption safety, CSV never-silently-drop, ReviewLog immutability) to a concrete, appropriately-scoped test layer rather than leaving test strategy as an afterthought discovered during build.
rejected_alternatives: Relying primarily on UI tests for correctness verification
Testing persistence only against the real on-device store rather than an in-memory container
constraints: tech_specs and build phases must map each locked correctness requirement to one of these four test layers explicitly

decisions.decision: Architecture is concretely implemented as two local Swift packages (RecallScheduling, RecallCSV) for pure domain logic plus an app-target SwiftData repository layer and SwiftUI+@Observable presentation, giving the already-locked three-layer architecture a specific file/module layout.
decisions.rationale: Codex and Claude independently produced compatible, near-identical package/module breakdowns; making it concrete now (not just 'physically separate' in prose) is what actually lets parallel build lanes compile independently.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving package boundaries as a stated principle without a concrete file layout for build lanes to follow
constraints: Build phase must create RecallScheduling and RecallCSV as real local SPM package targets, each with its own Swift Testing target

decisions.decision: Stats aggregation (forecast/history/retention) runs in a dedicated background StatsComputationActor (@ModelActor) with its own read-only ModelContext, triggered by ModelContext.didSave notifications and publishing into a @MainActor @Observable StatsCache — explicitly named as a concurrency domain separate from the main-actor synchronous grade-save write path.
decisions.rationale: Claude's addition: without this explicit separation, a builder reaching for the 'obviously simple' pattern would compute stats inline in a chart view's body, causing a full ReviewLog table scan on every re-render at the 300-3,000 card persona scale.
rejected_alternatives: Computing stats inline in view bodies or on the same main-actor write path as grade saves
constraints: Any future performance pass may not merge StatsComputationActor's read path back onto the main-actor write path

decisions.decision: UUID is the canonical identifier type across all cross-lane contracts (repositories, session snapshot queues, view models) — not SwiftData's PersistentIdentifier.
decisions.rationale: Codex's interfaces-json used UUID throughout while Claude's used PersistentIdentifier; as coordinator this is resolved to UUID because letting PersistentIdentifier leak into primary_ui/view-model types would require SwiftData imports outside the persistence layer, breaking the layer separation the whole architecture is built to enforce.
rejected_alternatives: Using PersistentIdentifier as the canonical cross-lane identifier
constraints: No primary_ui or services_utilities type may reference PersistentIdentifier directly; only the SwiftData repository implementations may translate between UUID and PersistentIdentifier internally

decisions.decision: The review session snapshot queue must tolerate a stale/missing card ID at grading time (e.g. a card deleted between session start and being graded) by skipping it, incrementing a visible staleSkippedCount, and continuing — never crashing and never fabricating a grade or a silently-shrunk summary.
decisions.rationale: Codex's Red Team catch: no prior phase named this edge case, and without an explicit test for it the app could still crash or silently misreport progress while claiming correctness, directly undermining the core trust promise.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving stale-ID handling as undefined/implicit behavior discovered during build
Treating a stale ID as a crash-worthy invariant violation
constraints: Build/test phase must include a dedicated stale-ID mid-session skip test
Session summary UI must be able to surface staleSkippedCount if nonzero rather than hiding the discrepancy

decisions.decision: CSVRowStatus is finalized as a concrete Swift enum with one case per malformed/duplicate/cap-blocked reason plus an ok case carrying the parsed front/back/note, replacing prose descriptions of the error taxonomy with a compiled shared contract type.
decisions.rationale: Both contributors converged on the same taxonomy; encoding it as a real type (not a string or prose list) is what makes 'never silently drop a row' independently checkable by both the parser and the preview UI.
rejected_alternatives: Representing row status as a loosely-typed string/reason pair instead of an enum
constraints: CSVParser.parseImportPreview and the import preview UI must both consume this exact enum, with no additional untyped error paths

decisions.decision: Navigation uses typed per-tab route enums (StudyRoute, StatsRoute, SettingsRoute) instead of a type-erased NavigationPath.
decisions.rationale: Claude's addition: gives parallel build lanes compile-time-checked routing instead of stringly-typed/type-erased paths that only fail at runtime.
rejected_alternatives: A single type-erased NavigationPath shared across all three tabs
constraints: Each tab's NavigationStack must be driven by its own typed route array, not a shared NavigationPath

decisions.decision: Plan-cap logic (deck/card counts vs. Free limits, StoreKit entitlement state) is centralized in one injected PlanGate object read by the card editor, CSV import preview, and deck creation flow.
decisions.rationale: Claude's addition: prevents three independently-implemented cap counters from drifting out of sync, which would otherwise be a real risk given caps are checked from three separate UI entry points.
rejected_alternatives: Letting each cap-checking screen compute deck/card counts independently
constraints: No screen may compute Free-tier cap state itself; all cap checks read from the single injected PlanGate instance

decisions.decision: Optional hardware keyboard shortcuts (space/return to reveal; 1-4 or arrow keys to grade Again/Hard/Good/Easy) are added to the review session as an additive acceleration layered on top of the existing tap-based GradeStaircase, with a discoverable hint row.
decisions.rationale: Claude's proposal: zero new frameworks, doesn't touch the locked non-color-dependent accessibility contract (VoiceOver/staircase labels remain the accessibility path of record), and is a direct, low-risk expression of the review-flow-speed priority for the daily, at-scale persona this app targets.
rejected_alternatives: Treating keyboard shortcuts as a replacement input path rather than additive
Deferring keyboard acceleration as out-of-scope polish
constraints: Keyboard shortcuts must never be the sole way to satisfy the non-color-dependent grading accessibility requirement; VoiceOver labels and reduced-motion behavior must remain unchanged regardless of input method

decisions.decision: Deck gains reminderHour/reminderMinute optional fields implementing per-deck Plus reminder-time override, and StatsSnapshot.retentionRate is typed as an optional Double (nil, not 0, when sampleSize is 0) to distinguish no-data from zero-retention.
decisions.rationale: Concrete schema/type-level implementation of two already-locked requirements (per-deck reminder customization as a Plus differentiator; honest empty vs. sparse stats states) that needed an actual field/type decision to be buildable.
rejected_alternatives: Storing retentionRate as 0.0 for both true zero-retention and no-data cases
Modeling per-deck reminder override as a separate join table instead of optional fields on Deck
constraints: UI layer must branch on retentionRate == nil for empty-state copy, distinct from a genuine low/zero retention value

decisions.decision: Testing strategy is given concrete named suites (RecallSchedulingTests, RecallCSVTests, RecallPersistenceTests, RecallIntegrationTests, RecallUITests) mapped to the architecture layers, with two new required cases beyond prior phases: stale-ID mid-session skip, and per-grade save-failure UI behavior (card stays visible, marked unsaved, retry — never a fake decrement or advance).
decisions.rationale: Turns the already-locked four-layer testing strategy from ios_architecture_review into buildable, named test targets and closes two edge cases (stale ID, save failure) that this phase surfaced but that weren't yet mapped to a specific test.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving stale-ID and save-failure behavior as implicit/undocumented edge cases discovered during manual QA
constraints: Build phase must add both new test cases to the CI-runnable suite, not treat them as optional manual checks

decisions.decision: Build sequencing is dependency-driven with the pure domain layer (RecallScheduling + RecallCSV, fully test-green including SM-2's day-boundary/DST/timezone matrix) as the hard gate before any milestone that reads or writes scheduling state (persistence repositories, review session, stats); scaffolding/shell work (package targets, three-tab shell, Theme.swift skeleton, ModelContainerFactory/AppRootState, PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy) has no dependency on SM-2 completion and can run in parallel with it.
decisions.rationale: All three contributors converged on this same critical-path structure independently; making the parallelizable scaffolding work explicit (rather than implying everything queues serially behind SM-2) shortens the actual critical path without weakening the correctness gate.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the roadmap as a strict serial queue where nothing starts until SM-2 is fully done
constraints: Any milestone touching Card.easeFactor/intervalDays/repetitionCount or ReviewLog writes must not start until RecallSchedulingTests and RecallCSVTests are fully green

decisions.decision: The force-quit interruption XCUITest and the stale-ID mid-session skip test are built as part of the review session milestone's definition of done, not appended afterward as a separate testing/polish milestone.
decisions.rationale: Both Codex and Claude agreed a session architecture not built with these tests in mind from the start isn't cheaply retrofittable; treating them as trailing QA tasks risks a session design that has to be reworked to accommodate them later.
rejected_alternatives: Building the review session UI first and adding interruption/stale-ID test coverage as a later hardening pass
constraints: The review session milestone cannot be marked complete without both tests passing, not just the happy-path UI working

decisions.decision: The domain-engine milestone reuses next_steps_small's validated SM-2/review-loop code if it exists and passes its own tests, porting it into RecallScheduling and adapting its public surface to the frozen tech_specs interfaces; if no such artifact exists, it is built fresh against those same interfaces. Either way, the deferred DST/timezone-crossing/external-cross-check test coverage (explicitly pushed to this phase by DEC-next_steps_small-005) is the actual net-new work in this milestone, not a full SM-2 rewrite.
decisions.rationale: Codex and Claude converged independently on this exact resolution in round 2; deciding it now removes an estimate-invalidating ambiguity that would otherwise let milestone 2's duration swing by days depending on which assumption task assignment happens to make.
rejected_alternatives: Always rewriting SM-2/review-loop code from scratch regardless of whether a validated artifact already exists
Leaving the reuse-vs-rebuild question implicit for the build phase to discover
constraints: Whichever path is taken, the resulting module must conform exactly to the SM2Engine/Grade/SchedulingState signatures already locked in tech_specs' interfaces-json

decisions.decision: The only fallback cut under schedule pressure is trimming CSV import (export stays); no must-have feature — including Free/Plus gating and cap enforcement — may be cut or disabled as a second-tier fallback, only should-have/could-have items may be deferred beyond the CSV-import cut.
