decisions.rationale: Claude's round-2 argument for cutting StoreKit/Plus gating as a second tier (monetization postdates the original prompt's six core features, and a lapsed-subscription-never-hides-data rule already makes 'no subscription' the limit case) was well-reasoned but conflicts with app_features' explicit, already-locked constraint that all eleven must-have groups — Free/Plus gating named among them — are non-negotiable completion gates that no future phase may downgrade; a scheduling contingency in this phase isn't grounds to override that boundary.
rejected_alternatives: Cutting StoreKit/Plus gating entirely as a second fallback tier, shipping every user the full uncapped app for free if time runs short beyond CSV import
constraints: Any future time-pressure decision must cite this fixed cut order rather than reopening which must-have is 'safe' to cut

decisions.decision: PlanGate is introduced at the persistence/repositories milestone as an injected singleton stub (isPlus hardcoded true, unlimited caps) before the card editor, CSV import preview, or deck creation flow are built, and becomes true entitlement-aware once the subscription milestone wires real StoreKit state into it.
decisions.rationale: Building the three cap-checking screens before PlanGate exists would reproduce the exact three-independently-drifting-cap-counters problem tech_specs already ruled out (DEC-tech_specs-007); standing up the stub early costs almost nothing since persistence already computes the deck/card counts PlanGate reads.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring PlanGate until the StoreKit/subscription milestone and retrofitting cap checks into the three already-built screens afterward
constraints: Card editor, CSV import preview, and deck creation must all read cap state from PlanGate from the milestone they are first built, never compute it independently even temporarily

decisions.decision: A dedicated spike proving StatsComputationActor's ModelContext.didSave-triggered cross-context refresh actually works (no race, no staleness) runs before the full forecast/history/retention aggregation is implemented, and a 3-second-under-3,000-cards/3-years-of-logs latency ceiling is written into that milestone's definition of done as a testable NFR.
decisions.rationale: Claude flagged this concurrency bridge as unprototyped and risky to discover mid-milestone; Gemini's round-1 latency ceiling ties directly to the daily-studier persona's card-count range from per_app_product_brief and both contributors agreed it belongs in the milestone's DoD rather than floating as an aside.
rejected_alternatives: Building the full stats aggregation directly on top of the interfaces-json signature without first proving the didSave bridge works
Treating the latency ceiling as an aspirational note rather than a gating test
constraints: Stats milestone cannot be marked complete without both the spike passing and the latency ceiling test passing under simulated load

decisions.decision: The authoritative interruption-safety test remains a genuine app.terminate() SIGKILL XCUITest per DEC-ios_architecture_review-005, unchanged; the flakiness mitigation is a test-only pause inserted immediately after the synchronous per-grade save call returns (before the queue index advances), which lets the external terminate() call reliably land inside that window, rather than a self-initiated app exit triggered by a diagnostic flag.
decisions.rationale: Gemini's original proposal (the app hard-exits itself on a diagnostic flag right after save) would prove the app chooses to die, not that it survives an uncooperative OS-level kill — a materially weaker claim than the locked requirement exists to prove; Claude's refinement gets the same determinism benefit by controlling only the timing of an externally-triggered, genuine terminate() call.
rejected_alternatives: A diagnostic flag causing the app to call its own hard exit as the flakiness-reduction mechanism
constraints: Any test-only pause/hook added for timing determinism must not itself terminate or exit the process; the kill must always originate from the XCUITest harness's app.terminate() call

decisions.decision: The haptic ladder is implemented exactly per DEC-design_handoff-009's mapping regardless of hardware availability; physical-device validation is tracked as a real dependency, and if this build environment turns out to be Simulator-only, that is logged as an explicit, named entry in the Gap & Limitations register rather than assumed complete or silently skipped.
decisions.rationale: Both Codex and Claude agreed waiting to confirm device availability before deciding isn't worth the delay; the honest default is to build to spec and disclose the unverified state if a physical device never becomes available, consistent with this project's standing priority on honest limitations over silent gaps.
rejected_alternatives: Blocking milestone acceptance indefinitely pending confirmation of physical-device availability
Marking haptic validation complete without ever having tested on real hardware
constraints: Gap & Limitations register must include the haptic-hardware-unverified disclosure by final stabilization if no physical device was used during the build

decisions.decision: Task assignment adopts the four fixed lanes (data_domain, primary_ui, services_utilities, polish_resilience) with a working draft of 33 tasks, but the draft is explicitly provisional pending round-2 reconciliation of directory naming, task granularity, and requirement-ID scheme.
decisions.rationale: Two substantive contributors (Codex, Claude) produced compatible but non-identical breakdowns of the same locked milestones; rather than pick one arbitrarily, the coordinator is carrying Claude's more granular draft forward as the working baseline since it's the more execution-ready of the two, while flagging the specific points of divergence for round 2 rather than silently resolving them.
rejected_alternatives: Locking Codex's 13-task coarse breakdown as final without addressing the fileSystemSynchronizedGroups mitigation or requirement-ID mismatch
Locking Claude's 33-task breakdown as final without giving Codex or Gemini a chance to contest the safety-test ownership call
constraints: Round 2 must explicitly resolve: Xcode project/directory naming (RecallIOS vs Recall), task granularity, ownership of the force-quit/stale-ID XCUITests, and requirement IDs cross-checked against app_features' locked 55-item list

decisions.decision: Repo layout roots directly at the writable workspace (Recall.xcodeproj, Recall/, Packages/, RecallTests/, RecallUITests/) with no nested recall-ios/ folder inside it.
decisions.rationale: The session's actual working directory is already .../recall-ios/.agent_cwd — recall-ios is already the containing folder one level up, so a second recall-ios/ layer inside the workspace would be redundant and lengthen every file path for no disambiguating benefit; verified against the real environment rather than decided by preference.
rejected_alternatives: Codex's recall-ios/Recall/... nested layout
constraints: All lane-owned files in this phase's tasks-json use paths relative to the workspace root with no recall-ios/ prefix

decisions.decision: Task granularity is locked to the 33-task fine-grained breakdown rather than the earlier 13-task coarse version.
decisions.rationale: Codex conceded in round 2 that mapping app_features' 52 must-have CORE requirements onto 13 tasks would produce acceptance-criteria lists deep enough to violate DEC-app_features-003's ban on restated-feature-description acceptance criteria; finer tasks are what make each criterion independently checkable.
rejected_alternatives: Codex's original 13-task coarse milestone breakdown
constraints: Each task's acceptance_criteria must remain independently pass/fail checkable, not a restatement of the task title

decisions.decision: The force-quit SIGKILL test, stale-ID/reorder tests, Gap & Limitations disclosure assertion, and final stabilization pass are owned by polish_resilience, deliberately separate from the primary_ui tasks that build the underlying review-session/gap-register features.
decisions.rationale: Both Codex and Claude converged on this: if the same lane under the same feature-delivery deadline both builds a safety-critical mechanism and grades whether it survives, the incentive produces technically-passing-but-weak tests (e.g. a kill timed too late, an assertion that only checks a count instead of which specific cards are gone).
rejected_alternatives: Bundling the force-quit and stale-ID tests into the same task as the review-session UI build (Codex's original round-1 proposal)
constraints: No future phase may reassign these tests to the feature-building lane to save coordination overhead

decisions.decision: Requirement IDs in this phase's tasks use the R-<CATEGORY>-<NNN> scheme; reconciling these against the canonical 55-item requirements.json from app_features is deferred to a mechanical checklist step inside final stabilization (T-033), not treated as a phase-blocking design question.
decisions.rationale: Neither contributor had the actual requirements.json in front of them in this room, so any scheme adopted now is provisional; the real work is a diff-and-match pass, which is an execution task, not a decision requiring more discussion rounds.
rejected_alternatives: Blocking phase consensus until the canonical requirement IDs are manually looked up and substituted
Leaving the REQ-* vs R-* mismatch from round 1 unresolved
constraints: T-033 must not be marked complete until every CORE requirement in the real requirements.json is cited by at least one task with zero orphans

decisions.decision: A CSV import flow must be added to flows-json alongside the existing export flow (F-004) before build starts.
decisions.rationale: All three participants (Codex, Claude, Gemini's fallback) independently flagged that CSV import — a primary promise with the most locked correctness surface (duplicate detection, cap-blocked rows, malformed-row taxonomy) — has no crawl-verifiable flow, unlike export.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving CSV import verification to unit/integration tests only, without a crawlable UI flow
constraints: flows-json must include an import flow exercising file selection, preview, and confirm-commit before this phase can close

decisions.decision: Recall/Services/GapRegisterEntry.swift needs an explicit single-owner/handoff resolution between T-004 (bootstrap skeleton) and T-030 (consolidate final content) rather than two lanes independently writing to the same file.
decisions.rationale: Codex and Gemini's fallback both identified this as a same-file collision risk that weakens the gap-register integrity requirement if left implicit.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving both tasks as independent writers to the same file with no explicit dependency
constraints: T-030 must be made an explicit continuation of T-004 (e.g., depends_on T-004 with ownership transfer noted), not a parallel write

decisions.decision: The canonical requirements.json must be authored and checked into the repo before T-001 starts; T-033's job changes from first-time authoring/reconciliation to a mechanical diff against that concrete artifact.
decisions.rationale: No content matching the '55-item canonical requirements.json' referenced since app_features actually appears anywhere in this project's history; what's adjacent to it is a mismatched, incompatible ID scheme from an unrelated repair exercise. Reconciling 52 CORE requirements against 33 tasks needs full context, and T-033 (the last task of a long multi-lane build) is the point in the process with the least context remaining, not the most.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring requirements.json authoring/reconciliation entirely to T-033 as originally planned
Assuming the file already exists without verifying it
constraints: requirements.json must exist as a real, checked-in artifact before T-001 begins
T-033 verifies zero orphaned CORE requirements against this artifact rather than authoring it for the first time

decisions.decision: A Free-tier 30-day stats-history window must be added as an enforced requirement: StatsComputationActor's forecast/history/retention queries take a windowing parameter sourced from PlanGate.isPlus (30 days for Free, unbounded for Plus), and the stats screens must visibly communicate when history is windowed rather than silently truncating it.
decisions.rationale: per_app_product_brief locked exactly two things Plus unlocks — no deck/card caps and no 30-day stats window — but only the cap side was wired into the task backlog (via PlanGate); the stats-history side had no owning task in T-019/T-020/T-021, meaning Plus would ship with only one of its two promised differentiators and Free users would silently get more than intended.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the 30-day stats cap unenforced and treating Free/Plus gating as satisfied by deck/card caps alone
Silently truncating history without visible indication, which would violate the project's own no-fabrication/honest-empty-state standard
constraints: T-020 acceptance criteria gain the windowing parameter sourced from PlanGate.isPlus
T-021 acceptance criteria gain a visible windowed-history indicator for Free users

decisions.decision: The GapRegisterEntry.swift collision is resolved concretely: T-030 is given an explicit depends_on T-004, and T-004 gains an acceptance criterion that its skeleton file must compile with placeholder entries, so T-030 extends a real file rather than racing a second writer to overwrite it.
decisions.rationale: Codex's refinement of the round-1 finding: 'same owner lane' isn't the same as an explicit ownership handoff, and without a dependency edge the file could still diverge before one writer wins, undermining the Gap register's own integrity as an auditable product promise.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving same-lane ownership as sufficient without a formal task dependency
Splitting GapRegisterEntry.swift into two separate files to avoid the collision entirely
constraints: Build phase must add T-030 -> depends_on -> T-004 to the task graph and add the compiling-skeleton criterion to T-004

decisions.decision: Incremental build-verification checkpoints are added at two points: after T-011 (persistence + SM-2 tests green) and after T-018 (review session + interruption tests green), where pass/fail on that slice is confirmed before primary_ui/services_utilities/polish_resilience proceed into stats, CSV, reminders, or StoreKit work.
decisions.rationale: Given the size of this single-pass build (pure SM-2 package with a DST/timezone/external-cross-check matrix, actor-based stats with an unprototyped concurrency spike, an app.terminate() SIGKILL test, StoreKit 2 with scripted subscription scenarios, a hand-rolled CSV parser, and an unverifiable-on-real-hardware haptic ladder), applying the project's own 'don't declare done until verification agrees' rule only at the final task (T-033) risks discovering a foundational flaw only after four more feature areas have been built on top of it.
rejected_alternatives: Running the full 33-task backlog with verification only at the end (T-033)
Checkpointing after every task, which would be excessive process overhead relative to the risk being managed
constraints: Build execution must report explicit pass/fail on the T-011 slice and the T-018 slice before downstream lanes proceed, without changing task count, order, or lane ownership

decisions.decision: The QA checklist explicitly sorts every feature into 'real and working,' 'honest placeholder,' or 'fully absent,' and tests each category on its own terms rather than applying one uniform pass/fail bar.
decisions.rationale: The app's entire promise is never lying about state; a QA script that tells a tester to tap a CSV import button that routes to a placeholder and call it a bug (or, worse, a script that pretends the placeholder is the real feature) would itself violate that promise inside the QA process.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all Settings features as equally testable end-to-end regardless of implementation status
Omitting placeholder/absent features from the checklist entirely
constraints: Any future QA pass must re-classify features into these three buckets before writing new test steps, since implementation status can change between builds

decisions.decision: The force-quit mid-session interruption test is written as an exact, numbered manual procedure (create deck, add 2 cards, grade one, kill within ~1s, relaunch, assert exact due split) rather than a one-line 'verify interruption safety' bullet.
decisions.rationale: Build verification's latest result shows RecallTests/ReviewSessionViewModelTests.swift fails to compile on a main-actor-isolation error, which means the automated XCUIApplication.terminate() force-quit test cannot currently run at all — making this manual walkthrough the only presently-executable proof of the app's single most important trust claim.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on the (currently non-functional) automated XCUITest as sufficient coverage
A vague one-line manual instruction to 'test force-quit'
constraints: This manual procedure must be re-run as a regression check after any future change to the review session or data layer, and treated as load-bearing until the automated test target compiles again

decisions.decision: QA steps are written in plain visual/behavioral language ('tap the first deck in the list') rather than referencing internal accessibility identifiers a human tester cannot see.
decisions.rationale: A checklist meant for a human tester to run without asking what to tap fails its own acceptance bar if it assumes knowledge of XCUITest identifiers from flows-json.
rejected_alternatives: Writing steps directly against the flows-json accessibility identifiers (study.deckCell_0, review.gradeGood, etc.)
constraints: Identifiers may be used only as a parenthetical cross-reference for automated-test authors, never as the primary instruction

decisions.decision: Non-color-dependent grading accessibility is tested literally, by switching the device to Grayscale or Smart Invert and confirming grade buttons remain distinguishable, rather than just visually inspecting the staircase layout.
decisions.rationale: The locked accessibility requirement is that grading works without relying on color; the only real proof is removing color from the display and confirming comprehension still holds, not just eyeballing that labels exist.
rejected_alternatives: Accepting visual inspection of the shape/label staircase as sufficient proof of the color-independence requirement
constraints: Any future accessibility regression check for grading should include a grayscale/Smart Invert pass, not just a VoiceOver pass

decisions.decision: Haptic-ladder verification is explicitly marked as requiring a physical device, and any 'pass' recorded from Simulator testing alone is invalid.
decisions.rationale: iOS Simulator does not produce real haptic feedback, so a tester feeling 'something' or nothing at all on Simulator provides no signal about the real ascending-intensity ladder; project history already flagged this as unverified on physical hardware.
rejected_alternatives: Accepting a Simulator-only run as sufficient haptic verification
constraints: QA reports must record Simulator vs. physical device explicitly for this check specifically

decisions.decision: Study tab and Stats screens are tested with three distinct empty/sparse/populated substates per screen (true-empty vs. all-caught-up vs. sparse vs. full data) rather than a single empty-vs-not-empty check.
decisions.rationale: These states carry different meaning to the user (no decks yet vs. nothing due today vs. not enough history yet) and were separately locked as distinct copy/design states in earlier design phases; collapsing them in QA would let a regression that merges these states back together go undetected.
rejected_alternatives: Treating 'empty' as a single binary state across Study and Stats
constraints: Future QA passes on these screens must continue checking each substate independently, with its own screenshot/expected copy

decisions.decision: V1 submission ships as a fully free app with zero subscription/Plus/paywall UI or marketing copy anywhere in the binary or App Store metadata; StoreKit/monetization is deferred to a future v1.1 submission once actually built and tested.
decisions.rationale: No StoreKit code, .storekit config, or Plan/Subscription screen exists anywhere in the codebase despite being a locked must-have in earlier phases; marketing a tier that doesn't exist in the binary is a guaranteed App Store metadata-mismatch rejection, and a rushed StoreKit integration risks tripping 3.1.2 (missing terms/privacy links, non-functional Restore Purchases, unhandled offline-purchase state) — all previously-flagged risks that were never closed.
rejected_alternatives: Submitting with Plus/subscription tier language despite no implementation
Shipping a disabled/greyed-out 'Upgrade' affordance as a placeholder
constraints: No later phase may add subscription/Plus copy to App Store metadata or in-app UI without a real, tested StoreKit implementation behind it
PlanGate's hardcoded-unlimited stub requires no functional change to support this decision

decisions.decision: App Store positioning is locked to 'Recall — the flashcard app that never lies to you': offline-forever, zero accounts, zero ads, provably-correct SM-2 engine, explicitly not competing on feature breadth or Stats/chart richness.
decisions.rationale: Both participants independently converged on the same trust-first framing, consistent with the project's design language ('The Honest Ledger') and its target audience of ex-Anki/Quizlet users who value reliability over engagement features.
rejected_alternatives: Leading marketing copy with Stats/chart features or breadth of functionality
Generic 'clean and modern flashcard app' positioning
constraints: Marketing copy and screenshots must not claim any capability (reminders scheduling, CSV import/export, subscriptions) that isn't actually live in the submitted build

decisions.decision: Privacy label is Data Not Collected across every category; PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy's existing Required Reason API declarations (UserDefaults, file timestamp) are accepted as sufficient and must be reconfirmed present in the actual built artifact before submission.
decisions.rationale: The app has zero network calls, no analytics, no third-party SDKs, and no tracking; the privacy manifest already on disk matches this reality, so the label should be the simplest possible truthful claim rather than over-declaring or under-declaring categories.
rejected_alternatives: Adding privacy categories not actually justified by real API usage
Skipping direct confirmation that PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy exists in the built artifact
constraints: Final build verification must directly confirm PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy is present and accurate before submission, not just assume it from architecture-phase intent

decisions.decision: Notification permission copy and gating remain exactly as currently implemented: user-initiated (gated behind toggling Reminders on, never at cold launch), and the ask explains only 'so we can tell you how many cards are due' with no card/deck content ever mentioned.
decisions.rationale: This already matches the locked non-nagging tone and the notification-content-privacy rule (count-only body text); no Info.plist usage-description string is required since the app touches no other permission-gated API (camera/location/contacts).
rejected_alternatives: Requesting notification permission at first launch
Adding marketing language implying richer notification content
constraints: Any future change to notification copy must preserve the count-only, no-content-leak rule

decisions.decision: Screenshot/storyboard assets must be captured from the real shipped UI using manually-seeded review history (since Demo Data seeding doesn't exist as a feature), including at least one populated Stats view, one dark-mode paired shot, and the Gap & Limitations screen itself as a legitimate differentiator rather than something to hide.
decisions.rationale: There is no Demo Data toggle to lean on for populated screenshots, and both participants agreed that showing the Gap & Limitations screen is honest evidence of the app's 'never lies to you' claim rather than a liability to obscure.
rejected_alternatives: Using placeholder/mocked data for screenshots
Omitting the Gap & Limitations screen from App Store assets
constraints: No App Store screenshot may depict functionality (working reminders, working CSV import/export, a subscription tier) that isn't actually live in the submitted build

decisions.decision: A real support/contact path (support URL or in-app contact) and legal-links entry point must be added before submission, since none currently exists and App Store Connect requires a working support URL at submission time.
decisions.rationale: Both participants independently flagged this as a real, concrete launch blocker rather than a nice-to-have — it's a hard App Store Connect submission requirement, not a design preference.
rejected_alternatives: Submitting without a support URL and addressing it only if rejected
constraints: This must be resolved before submission, not treated as a post-launch follow-up

decisions.decision: A two-tier launch-blocker framework is locked: honest 'not yet available' placeholders (CSV export/import, Demo Data) are tracked gaps that do not block App Store submission; features whose interactive UI appears fully functional but silently fails to deliver (Reminders) are treated as genuine launch blockers requiring resolution, not documentation.
decisions.rationale: Run through the project's own fixed tiebreaker (SM-2 correctness > review-flow speed > honest empty states), a clearly-labeled placeholder is priority-3 working exactly as designed, while a working-looking control that silently produces nothing is the one place that priority is actually at risk of being violated — these are not the same failure mode and shouldn't get the same treatment.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all incomplete features (placeholders and look-complete-but-silent ones alike) as equally launch-blocking
Treating all incomplete features as equally acceptable to ship with just a disclosure sentence
constraints: Any future phase classifying an incomplete feature must place it in one of these two tiers explicitly, not leave it ambiguous

decisions.decision: The Reminders feature's interactive Settings UI (toggle, permission request, time picker) is removed entirely for v1 rather than shipped as-is or fixed with a real scheduler under submission time pressure; it is replaced with a plain 'coming in a future update' line or folded into the Gap & Limitations register, and revisited alongside StoreKit in a v1.1 pass.
decisions.rationale: This exact feature has been confidently reported as fully built across nine-plus separate build_coordination/write_tests iterations, and every single time the ReminderScheduler turned out not to exist on disk — that history makes 'build it now, in time for submission' a real, demonstrated scheduling risk rather than a hypothetical one, whereas hiding one Settings row and adding one honest line carries near-zero engineering risk and is airtight honest.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping the Reminders UI as-is with an added clarifying disclosure sentence (initial Codex position, later retracted)
Building a minimal real ReminderScheduler now to keep the feature in v1
constraints: The App Store description, screenshot plan, and in-app copy must not reference reminders/notifications as a feature of this release
Any future v1.1 reminders work must be scoped as new feature work, not a quick fix to existing UI

decisions.decision: The screenshot/storyboard plan and App Store description are updated to drop any Reminders-related shot or copy, consistent with pulling that UI from v1.
decisions.rationale: A decision to remove a feature's UI has no effect if the marketing assets still depict or describe it — this closes that gap explicitly rather than leaving it as an implied follow-through.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the previously-planned Reminders screenshot/copy in place despite the UI being removed
constraints: Final asset review before submission must confirm no reminders reference remains in screenshots or description

decisions.decision: Final launch-blocker list for this submission is: (1) remove the interactive Reminders UI per DEC-app_store_readiness-008, (2) fix the RecallTests/ReviewSessionViewModelTests.swift main-actor-isolation compile error, (3) add a real support/contact URL both in App Store Connect metadata and as an in-app Settings route. CSV/Demo-Data placeholders and the absence of StoreKit are explicitly non-blocking tracked gaps for this release.
decisions.rationale: Synthesizes both rounds' agreement into one concrete, actionable list rather than leaving 'launch blockers' as a matter of interpretation between the two tiers established in DEC-app_store_readiness-007.
rejected_alternatives: Including CSV/Demo-Data incompleteness in the launch-blocker list
Declaring the app store-ready before the compile error and support URL are resolved
constraints: The app must not be declared App-Store-submission-ready until all three items in this list are actually resolved, not just planned

decisions.decision: Final verdict for this submission is NO-GO, pending direct confirmation (not assumption) that the three app_store_readiness launch blockers — Reminders interactive UI removal, the ReviewSessionViewModelTests.swift compile fix, and a real support/contact URL — were actually executed in code.
decisions.rationale: Those three items were decided, not built, in the immediately preceding phase; the latest verification block still shows the identical compile failure that motivated one of them, and there is no build phase between app_store_readiness and this review to have applied the other two.
rejected_alternatives: Declaring go based on the prior phase's decision alone, treating a decision as equivalent to its execution
Silently re-describing the three blockers as already resolved
constraints: Any future phase or build pass must directly verify (file existence, compile success, screen content) each of the three blockers rather than citing the app_store_readiness decision as proof they happened

decisions.decision: 'Compiled cleanly' and 'tests pass' are recorded as two distinct claims in this review, with only the first ever having been true anywhere in this project's history; the test target currently cannot compile at all, meaning the app's core interruption-safety guarantee has never been confirmed by a real automated run.
decisions.rationale: Six-plus build waves of confident 'verified'/'tested' language in this project's history all bottom out in manual code-tracing or a compile-only result, never a green xcodebuild test or swift test run; conflating the two would misrepresent the actual strength of evidence behind the app's central trust claim.
rejected_alternatives: Treating 'compiled cleanly' as sufficient grounds to call the interruption-safety guarantee proven
Repeating prior phases' confident test-pass language without re-checking it
constraints: Any future phase citing test coverage as evidence must distinguish a real executed test result from a hand-traced or compile-only claim

decisions.decision: Prompt coverage is reported honestly as a real, material scope reduction — roughly half of the six named core features (CSV UI wiring, Demo Data, local reminders, Free/Plus monetization) are missing, unwired, or removed for this release — rather than folded into soft 'known limitations' phrasing that undersells the gap.
decisions.rationale: The review's job per this phase's own playbook is to not hide unfinished work; describing this as the full six-feature build with minor gaps would misrepresent how much of the original prompt is actually reachable by a user today.
rejected_alternatives: Describing the gaps as minor polish items alongside the working core loop
Omitting Free/Plus and Demo Data absence from the headline coverage assessment since they were separately deprioritized in earlier phases
constraints: Any future phase or user-facing summary of this build must state the CSV-UI, Demo Data, reminders, and monetization gaps explicitly as prompt-coverage shortfalls, not just as tracked internal gaps

rejected_alternatives: Inventing portfolio-structure checks against a single-app project
Treating the empty sandboxed working directory shown in this room as evidence of a missing or misplaced project
constraints: Canonical audit path for any future structural check is /Users/pchordia/Documents/iOS-App-Factory/recall-ios/app_build
This audit result must not be read as production-readiness sign-off; it is silent on the standing NO-GO verdict from final_review

decisions.decision: Backfill readiness for Jira/Notion is specified as multiple discrete, differently-weighted tickets rather than a single 'Recall v1 — Done' item: blocking tickets for the three unresolved app_store_readiness launch blockers, a standalone ticket for getting a real swift test run to completion, and separate non-blocking post-launch backlog items for CSV UI wiring, Demo Data, StoreKit/Plus, and the SM-2 DST/external-cross-check tests.
decisions.rationale: A single closed ticket would misrepresent the project's real state given final_review's explicit NO-GO verdict and the material scope reduction against the original six-feature prompt; splitting the backfill preserves that honesty for downstream tracking.
rejected_alternatives: A single consolidated 'done' ticket for the whole app
Folding all remaining gaps into one generic 'known limitations' backlog item

decisions.decision: study.addDeckButton is assigned to the persistent/toolbar Add Deck control (always visible regardless of deck count), not to study.empty.action.
decisions.rationale: The empty-state CTA only exists with zero decks and disappears once one is created, so it cannot serve as a re-runnable canonical flow entry point across repeated crawl runs; the toolbar control is stable across deck count.
rejected_alternatives: Putting study.addDeckButton on study.empty.action
constraints: study.empty.action must not be renamed or removed since other already-passing flows may depend on it

decisions.decision: The fix must enumerate and resolve all identifiers named by the full declared flow (the '+6 more'), verified directly against docs/ui_crawl.json, before being considered complete — not just the first named failing step.
decisions.rationale: The prompt's control list is truncated to the first failure; the remaining six are highly likely to be inside the deck/card editor (front/back/note fields, save button), and patching only step 1 would let the crawl die one level deeper on the next run.
rejected_alternatives: Treating step 1's fix (Add Deck identifier) as sufficient to close this phase
constraints: Implementer must open docs/ui_crawl.json / the flow's step list before writing code, not infer identifiers solely from the truncated control list in this prompt

decisions.decision: This phase is scoped strictly to accessibility-identifier and control-wiring changes on already-functional UI; no changes to SM-2/scheduling, the review-session snapshot/queue, PlanGate, CSV, or StoreKit.
decisions.rationale: A crawl failing on a missing identifier is a labeling gap on working UI, not evidence of a functional or architectural defect, and touching those other systems would violate this phase's own bounded-change mandate.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing incidental touches to review-session or persistence code while in the area
constraints: Any future phase reviewing this change should flag scope creep into those systems as a violation of this decision

decisions.decision: RecallTests/ReviewSessionViewModelTests.swift's main-actor isolation compile error is fixed in the same pass by annotating the test type (or the specific initializer call) @MainActor, since a target that cannot compile means the release gate cannot run at all.
decisions.rationale: This is bundled with the UI-crawl fix because both are 'the gate literally cannot execute' problems, and the fix itself is small and separable from the identifier changes with no behavioral risk.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring the compile fix to a separate phase
constraints: Fix must not touch the review session's actual queue/snapshot logic, only the test's actor isolation

decisions.decision: 'Ensure all tests pass' is scoped to: get the suite compiling and executing, then report the real, per-test pass/fail result honestly — any failure that surfaces and is unrelated to the named compile error is reported as a separate, individually-named finding, not folded into either 'fixed' or 'still broken' for the UI-crawl issue, and does not block this phase's own acceptance criteria.
decisions.rationale: This project's own history (final_review) found every prior 'tests pass' claim traced back to a compile-only check or hand-tracing, never a real green run — this may be the first time the suite actually executes, and pre-existing failures unrelated to this fix shouldn't be laundered into either a false 'all green' claim or used to block an unrelated, already-scoped fix.
rejected_alternatives: Treating 'ensure all tests pass' as requiring this phase to fix every failure the first real test run surfaces
Silently reporting all-green without distinguishing real execution from compile-only success
constraints: Any future phase citing test results from this pass must distinguish real executed results from compile-only claims, per DEC-final_review-002

decisions.decision: The study.addDeckButton crawl fix from iterate_scope/build_coordination is confirmed closed and correct — verified via direct grep of the shipped toolbar/Group structure, not re-litigated — and should not be reopened by future phases.
decisions.rationale: The integrator found and fixed the actual root cause (toolbar scoped only to the non-empty branch, invisible on the exact fresh-install state the crawl starts from) rather than patching the symptom, and this was independently confirmed by both reviewers this round.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the crawl fix as still open or unverified pending further review
constraints: Future phases should treat this specific flow/identifier as resolved and focus verification effort on the three named follow-ups instead

decisions.decision: Overall release verdict remains NO-GO despite the crawl fix passing, because the Reminders UI is fully interactive but silently schedules nothing, CSVParser silently drops a class of legitimate import rows, and no real xcodebuild test/swift test execution has ever occurred in this project.
decisions.rationale: A narrow gate-fix passing is not the same claim as the app being safe to hand to a real user; the Reminders silent-no-op is exactly the look-functional-but-lies failure mode this app's own premise exists to prevent, and it remains live and untouched (correctly, per this phase's own scope lock) in the shipped build.
rejected_alternatives: Issuing a clean GO on the strength of the crawl fix and compile success alone
Issuing an unqualified NO-GO that fails to credit the crawl fix as genuinely done
constraints: Any future phase citing this review as evidence of readiness must preserve the distinction between 'this cycle's fix worked' and 'the app is release-ready' rather than blurring them

decisions.decision: Three concrete, owned follow-ups are set for the next cycle: fix CSVParser's header-collision silent-drop with an explicit CSVRowStatus case (CSV/domain lane), remove or truly wire the Reminders feature (services/notifications lane), and get a real xcodebuild test/swift test execution reported per-test including the force-quit interruption test (test/QA lane).
decisions.rationale: The phase playbook requires every blocker to have an owner or concrete next step; these three are the load-bearing gaps left after this cycle's narrow fix, each independently flagged by multiple reviewers across phases.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving these as generic 'known limitations' without lane ownership or a concrete action
constraints: The next build phase should scope explicitly to these three items rather than reopening the already-closed identifier-wiring fix

decisions.decision: This iterate_scope run is scoped exclusively to the visual QA failure on main_dark.png (and confirming main_light.png is clean); it must not reopen or re-touch the accessibility-identifier wiring work (study.addDeckButton, study.deckCell_0, tabBar.statsTab, tabBar.settingsTab) from the prior iterate_scope cycle, which DEC-final_review-004 already confirmed closed and correct.
decisions.rationale: The two cycles were triggered by different gates (UI-crawl vs. visual QA) and the decisions log explicitly warns against relitigating the already-closed identifier fix; Codex's round-1 proposal conflated the two.
rejected_alternatives: Re-wiring study.addDeckButton and tab bar identifiers as part of this pass per Codex's round-1 plan
constraints: No changes to any accessibility identifier confirmed closed by DEC-final_review-004 may be made in this pass

decisions.decision: Before any code change, the build phase must directly open docs/screenshots/main_light.png, docs/screenshots/main_dark.png, and docs/visual_qa.json and record in plain language the specific visible defect; the fix must target that named defect, not an inferred/guessed one.
decisions.rationale: A gemma3:4b BAD/score-50 verdict alone is too weak and noisy a signal to design a fix against without visual confirmation, and this project's history shows a repeated pattern of confident fixes for problems nobody actually verified.
rejected_alternatives: Inferring the likely dark-mode contrast defect from Theme.swift conventions and patching without opening the actual screenshots
constraints: Any future phase citing this fix as resolved must show the named defect and its resolution, not just a rerun-clean gate

decisions.decision: The fix is confined to Theme.swift's semantic color-token definitions and, at most, the styling of the single view rendering the failing screen; no layout redesign, no new components, no identifier changes.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the change bounded and consistent with the project's locked rule that colors route through Theme.swift as semantic light/dark roles rather than scattered literals or one-off view overrides.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing broader view-level restructuring if the defect looks structural rather than token-based, without first reporting it as a scope finding
constraints: If the real defect can't be resolved within Theme.swift + one view, it must be reported honestly as exceeding this pass's scope rather than silently expanded

decisions.decision: The dark-mode CTA visual-QA fix (EmptyStateView routing through surfaceElevated/textPrimary instead of the system amber accent) is confirmed as a real, correctly-scoped, compiling fix, but is recorded as evidentially strong rather than gate-confirmed, since docs/visual_qa.json has never been re-run against it.
decisions.rationale: No tooling in this pipeline can regenerate main_light.png/main_dark.png or re-execute the grader, so 'likely fixed the flagged defect' and 'gate passes' must remain distinct claims per this project's standing DEC-final_review-002 rule against conflating strong evidence with actual execution.
rejected_alternatives: Declaring the visual QA gate formally passed on the strength of the source-level fix alone
constraints: Any future phase citing this fix as gate-passing must show an actual re-run of docs/visual_qa.json against a fresh capture, not just the code-level justification recorded here

decisions.decision: Overall release verdict remains NO-GO, unchanged from DEC-final_review-005, with a fourth follow-up added: get the visual-QA screenshot-capture/grade tooling to actually run once against the current build so main_dark.png's status can be confirmed rather than inferred.
decisions.rationale: The dark-mode CTA fix, while real and well-evidenced, does not touch the three standing blockers (Reminders silent no-op, CSV silent-drop, no real test execution) that drove the prior NO-GO, so the verdict cannot flip on the strength of this narrow fix alone.
rejected_alternatives: Issuing a GO based on the CTA fix and compile-clean verification alone
Treating the CTA fix as sufficient grounds to consider the visual-QA gate closed
constraints: Any future phase must continue to distinguish 'this cycle's fix worked' from 'the app is release-ready,' per DEC-final_review-005
The next phase touching this app should prioritize the four owned follow-ups (CSV silent-drop, Reminders no-op, real test execution, visual-QA gate re-run) over any further narrow visual polish

decisions.decision: The seven failing crawl flows and six reported dead-tap/back-nav bugs are fixed in one bounded pass, split into two explicit treatment classes: Class 1 (pure additive accessibility-identifier attachments on tab items, deck cells, empty-state action buttons, and card-editor fields) and Class 2 (five dead taps + one back-nav violation, each individually traced to file/line and classified as either 'wiring fixed' or 'functional gap logged as out-of-scope follow-up', never collapsed into a blanket claim).
decisions.rationale: Splits a labeling-gap fix (safe, no behavior risk) from real dead-control/misnavigation bugs (a trust-relevant defect class for an app whose whole premise is never lying about state), preventing the crawl from being made to pass while a real defect stays hidden behind a newly-added identifier.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all seven flow failures and six dead-tap/back-nav reports as one undifferentiated 'wiring' fix
Adding identifiers without individually tracing and classifying each dead tap
constraints: Implementer must open docs/ui_crawl.json for the full step list of every declared flow before writing identifier code, per DEC-iterate_scope-002
Each of the 5 dead taps and 1 back-nav violation must be reported individually with file/line and a wiring-fixed vs out-of-scope classification

No changes outside AppShellView.swift, StateStateViews.swift, DeckDetailView.swift, StudyRootView.swift, deck-cell views, card-editor view, and RecallTests/ReviewSessionViewModelTests.swift (per DEC-iterate_scope-004)

decisions.decision: study.deckCell_0 is made discoverable purely by adding index-based accessibility identifiers to deck-list rows; if the 'Complete a review session end to end' flow has no deck-creation step before tapping this cell, that is reported as a flow-definition gap, not fixed by seeding fake demo data.
decisions.rationale: Fabricating a deck row to satisfy a crawl precondition would violate the project's own locked empty-state-honesty rule; the actual defect (if any) is in the flow's precondition, not the UI's identifier coverage.
rejected_alternatives: Seeding a fake/demo deck row so study.deckCell_0 always resolves
Assuming without checking that the flow already includes a deck-creation precondition
constraints: Any future phase discovering the flow lacks a deck-creation precondition must log it as a flow-definition finding, not silently patch it with seeded data

decisions.decision: Overall release verdict remains NO-GO, unchanged from DEC-final_review-005/008, despite the keyboard-first deck/card creation flow fix being genuine and independently traced.
decisions.rationale: A narrow, well-verified UI fix to the exact named gate failure does not resolve the standing blockers (unresolved dead-taps/back-nav across three phases, an unsettled Reminders live/dead contradiction, CSV silent-drop, and a never-once-executed real test suite) that this project's own review history has repeatedly identified as the actual gap between 'looks right' and 'proven right.'
rejected_alternatives: Issuing a GO on the strength of the keyboard-first flow fix and clean compile alone
Folding the newly-found gaps (skipped precondition check, Reminders contradiction) into generic known-limitations language instead of naming them as blockers

decisions.decision: The keyboard-first deck/card creation flow (deckDetail.addCardButton and the full Add Deck -> editor -> save -> deck cell -> deck detail -> add card -> card editor chain) is confirmed closed and correct via direct source trace, and should not be re-opened absent evidence of a genuine regression.
decisions.rationale: The integrator traced every hop to real navigation and action code (not matching identifier strings), giving this the same evidentiary strength as the previously-closed study.addDeckButton fix.
rejected_alternatives: Treating this fix as still provisional pending a fresh crawl run
constraints: Future phases should focus verification effort on the standing blockers rather than re-verifying this already-confirmed flow

decisions.decision: DEC-iterate_scope-010's acceptance check (whether the review-session flow has a deck-creation step before tapping study.deckCell_0) was not performed in this cycle's build_coordination pass and is recorded as an unmet, still-open acceptance criterion, not assumed satisfied.

rejected_alternatives: Assuming the precondition check was implicitly covered by the general flow trace and treating it as satisfied
constraints: Whoever next touches Study/review-session flows must explicitly confirm or deny this precondition and report the result, not skip it again

decisions.decision: A newly-surfaced, unresolved contradiction is logged: DEC-app_store_readiness-008 required removing the interactive Reminders UI entirely for v1, but this cycle's build_coordination lane report (Claude B) describes that same UI as fully live and functioning; this must be settled by a direct grep of SettingsView/ReminderScheduler before any future GO call, not assumed resolved in either direction.

Assuming the lane report's present-tense description means removal never happened, without checking

rejected_alternatives: Issuing a GO on the strength of the tab-bar fix and clean compile alone
Folding the unresolved Reminders contradiction and the still-open study.deckCell_0 precondition into generic known-limitations language instead of naming them as blockers with owners

The Reminders live/dead contradiction (DEC-final_review-012) must be the first thing the next phase touching Settings/Reminders actually checks via direct source grep, not deferred a fourth time

decisions.decision: DEC-final_review-012's required check (direct grep of SettingsView/ReminderScheduler to resolve the Reminders live/dead contradiction) was skipped again this cycle, not merely left open by environment limitation, and is escalated as the single highest-priority item for the next phase touching this app.

Allowing this check to be deferred to a fourth review cycle without explicit escalation
